- **Phase 386**: closes the second AKGEN research-audit item,
  `runtime_mechanics.valhalla`'s own real mechanics -- correcting three
  confirmed bugs in the already-wired Gate Angel machinery
  (`turn/cast_execution.py`) and replacing a placeholder in
  `turn/valhalla_execution.py` with the real, source-confirmed
  algorithm.
  - **Contention resolution, corrected**: `_gate_angel_register_
    candidate()` used to do reservoir sampling for a *uniformly* random
    winner among same-turn, same-due-alignment candidates. AKGEN's own
    confirmed rule is simpler and non-uniform: "first cast occupies the
    slot; every later cast has 50% to be nullified and 50% to replace
    the current incumbent" -- for `n` candidates this makes the *last*
    win with probability 1/2, the second-to-last 1/4, geometrically back
    to the *first*, who ties the second at the tail (never getting an
    own "replace" roll, only survival rolls) -- hand-derived and
    verified before coding.
  - **Alignment eligibility, corrected**: Divine and Undead Kingdoms
    used to be excluded from Gate Angel outright. AKGEN's own confirmed
    `validation_alignment_mapping` clamps them instead ("Divine counts
    as Good and Undead as Evil"), via a new `_gate_angel_clamped_
    alignment()`.
  - **Rotation reset, corrected**: `_gate_angel_due_alignment()`'s own
    5-alignment cycle now also force-resets on the `turn_number % 5 ==
    4` boundary (AKGEN's own second, independent reset condition),
    not only once all 5 alignments have actually been visited --
    matters when a turn passes with no Gate Angel cast at all.
  - **Visitor selection, real algorithm**: `turn/valhalla_execution.py`
    used to pick a uniformly random hero from the winning alignment's
    roster every time. AKGEN's own confirmed `visitor_selection` says
    turns 1-5 always use the roster's own *final* record -- verified,
    not just plausible: every one of this project's own 5

- **Phase 424**: the missing orchestration layer -- every
  individual stage (parser, world generation, `turn_processor.
  run_turn()`, `describe_turn_results()`) was already real and tested,
  but nothing tied them into one runnable "process a turn" pipeline, and
  `GameState` had no way to persist between turns at all. Answers "is
  this playable yet?" with a real, working answer: yes, turn-by-turn,
  via three new top-level modules and a real CLI.
  - New `persistence.py`: `save_game_state()`/`load_game_state()`,
    pickle-based. Documented why pickle, not JSON, and why not a
    reproduction of the original (unavailable, per `turn/kingdom_
    bridge.py`'s own docstring) save format -- every model here is a
    plain `@dataclass` with `HexCoord`/enum-keyed `dict`/`set` fields,
    exactly what `pickle` round-trips for free and JSON cannot without
    a large bespoke encode/decode layer that would itself be new,
    unsourced code. Documented real limits: no forward/backward
    compatibility promise across model changes, and the standard
    `pickle.load`-on-untrusted-input security caveat.
  - New `orchestrator.py`: `process_turn(state, order_file_paths,
    board_width=..., rng=...) -> TurnOutcome`. Parses every `.K1` move
    file (`parser/k1_moves.py parse_k1_moves_file()`), syncs each
    kingdom's real move-file data into `state` (`turn/kingdom_bridge.py
    sync_leaders_from_kingdom()`), combines every kingdom's leaders into
    one flat list (`run_turn()`'s own same-phase Multiple Contingents
    detection needs every kingdom in the same call, not one call per
    kingdom), dispatches the turn, and narrates it
    (`describe_turn_results()`). Explicitly scoped to one combined
    turn narrative, not personalized per-King letters -- the real
    `^B`/`^E` King-exclusion "narrator perspective" system
    `report/turn_report.py`'s own Phase 96/108 addenda already document
    as elided rather than guessed at is a separate, unbuilt feature,
    not silently faked here.

    --out save.pkl` (builds each King's own `KingdomState`/`LeaderState`
    from a caller-supplied JSON roster -- name/race/alignment/home
    province, the same data `worldgen/generate_new_game.py KingSetup`'s
    own docstring already says this project has no source to invent --
    then runs the real, sourced `generate_new_game()` pipeline) and
    `python -m ak_engine.cli run-turn --state save.pkl --orders *.K1
    --board-width W --report report.txt` (the repeatable per-turn step:
    `process_turn()`, write the narrative, save the updated state,

    `king_not_identified` warnings to stderr instead of them silently

  All three share one real "close encounter" dispatcher, mapped onto
  this project's `turn/challenge_execution.py execute_challenge()` --
  the personal CHALLENGE encounter (rulebook [3.12]), not `turn/
  duel.py`'s Supreme Commander duel (the user's own initial guess,
  corrected after research showed the source names no battle/command
  context, only a generic personal encounter, matching the "Captain of
  the Musketeers"/personal-swordplay theme). A new helper,
  `_apply_duel_encounter_merit()`, is called from each of `execute_
  challenge()`'s four outcomes:
  - **Ordinary refusal** (`accepted=False`): Duellist stake is 1 (not
    2, the "avoided" case) -- challenger +1, refusing target -1.

    points never recovered, zero for an unscathed win) -- not a
    transfer; nobody else's Bravest total changes.

  Two real rules: (1) ordinals 18/19 (`Discovery.HIEROGLYPHIC_
  TRANSLATION`/`Discovery.SCIENTIFIC_METHOD`) are permanently excluded
  from ordinary research -- only obtainable via starting equipment or
  trade; (2) a "world diffusion bias" -- a candidate discovery already
  owned by *some* Kingdom in the world (`GameState.discoveries_first_
  found_by`, already tracked permanently) is always kept, but a
  candidate no Kingdom has ever owned is kept only 5% of the time
  (`DISCOVERY_WORLD_DIFFUSION_KEEP_CHANCE`), rerolling 95% of the time --
  biasing the world toward discoveries that already exist somewhere
  rather than spreading first-ever discoveries evenly.

  parameter (its one caller, `_roll_sage_device_discovery()`, already had
  `state` in scope); the reroll loop is capped at 200 attempts

  bound guaranteeing termination, not a sourced magnitude.

  per-ability credit accumulator, sourced from `AKGEN_reverse_
  engineering_report (2).md` SS2/SS6 -- supersedes Phase 44's original
  single-threshold-roll design now that a real source is available.

  Real per-`PR` sequence: (1) roll the aptitude gate,
  `roll_practice_aptitude_gate()` -- `P = 2^-max(0, target_skill -
  aptitude)`, identical to Phase 44's own halving curve, just no longer
  scaled by a separate per-context "base chance" first (the real engine
  has none: solo/tied/guaranteed-if-lower all roll the exact same gate).
  (2) On gate **failure**, the existing `APT_RISE_CHANCE[current_skill]`
  aptitude-increase roll fires, unchanged from Phase 44. (3) On gate

  skill rises *immediately*, same as before; otherwise the attempt earns
  **persistent credit** toward that ability -- `PRACTICE_CREDIT_TIED_
  GAIN` (10) if tied with a co-practicer this phase, `PRACTICE_CREDIT_
  SOLO_GAIN` (5) if solo -- stored in new `LeaderState.practice_credit:
  dict[int, int]` (keyed by `Ability.value`). Once a practicer's own
  credit for that ability reaches `PRACTICE_CREDIT_RISE_THRESHOLD` (100),
  the skill rises immediately and 100 is subtracted -- no second gate
  roll needed for the threshold-crossing attempt itself.

  `practice_credit` is deliberately **not** merged into `SkillTable.
  raw_values` (which mirrors real GW file bytes, including an
  already-documented unexplained 31st trailing value) -- this counter has
  no confirmed real-file representation to preserve, so it stays a pure
  in-memory field. Documented in its own docstring as sharing the real
  byte with `Add_Experience`, which this project doesn't implement (no
  combat/movement/cast-triggered skill growth exists yet, only Practice).

  PRACTICE_CHANCE` and `attempt_skill_rise()`/`_chance_after_aptitude_
  halving()` are removed (the real gate has no per-context base chance to
  halve); `APT_RISE_CHANCE`/`MAX_SKILL_LEVEL` are unchanged. New
  `roll_practice_aptitude_gate()` replaces the old fused gate-and-rise
  function; a new internal `_resolve_practice_attempt()` is the shared
  core every context (solo/pair/group) now calls.

  **Design choice**: `resolve_practice_solo`/`_pair`/`_group` still take
  raw `(skill, aptitude, credit)` values, not `LeaderState` directly, even
  though the real formula is credit-based -- `execute_practice_group()`'s
  own Phase 310 comatose gate must leave a comatose co-practicer's stored
  state completely untouched (skill, aptitude, *and now credit*) while
  still using their *pre-attempt* skill in the group's own tied/minimum
  comparison; keeping the resolvers pure functions of frozen input values
  lets the comatose gate skip persisting a resolver's output for exactly
  one practicer without ever touching `LeaderState` inside the resolver
  itself. See `practice_execution.py`'s own module docstring for the full
  rationale.

  `tally_emperor_vote()` rewritten off `AKGEN_reverse_engineering_report
  (2).md` SS13.3/SS13.5 -- supersedes this module's original design
  (Phase 228) of comparing a candidate's share against the sum of
  *expressed* ballots only.

  election_vote_weight()` summed, **including non-voters/abstainers**.
  A candidate wins immediately once their running share (accumulated by
  scanning ballots in ascending voter-Kingdom-ID order) exceeds 50% of
  `V_world` -- the real engine's own early-exit, so `votes_by_candidate`
  may reflect only a partial tally when an early win is found, not every
  ballot. If nobody clears 50% outright, whoever has the single highest
  share that still clears the **time-decaying** threshold `R`
  (`election_threshold_percent()`, already correct, already used for the
  *request*-to-call-a-vote gate -- directly reused, no new formula
  needed) wins instead, ties broken by whichever candidate's share was
  the first (in ascending voter-scan order) to reach the eventual best
  value. `tally_emperor_vote()` gains a required `current_turn`
  parameter (its one caller, `resolve_emperor_election()`, already
  receives `vote_turn` and forwards it). `ElectionResult.total_votes_
  cast` now holds `V_world`, not a sum of cast ballots (docstring
  updated, field name kept to avoid a wider ripple).

  formulas, new `turn/druidic_monster_aid.py`, sourced from `AKGEN_

  early the moment `q` goes even, clamped to ordinals 0-8
  (`Alignment.DIVINE`..`Alignment.MECHANICAL` -- `Alignment.SPECIAL`,
  ordinal 9, is never a reachable walk endpoint, matching this project's
  other Alignment-ordinal tables' own confirmed gap for it).
  `monster_join_probability()`: `d_D >= d_E` (the effective alignment's
  own distance from Druidic is no smaller than its distance from the
  enemy) means 0% eligible -- including the degenerate Druidic-vs-

  `1 - d_D/d_E`. `monster_strength_bonus()`: `floor(hit_points *
  (melee_damage + missile_damage) / 50)` -- the Gold Dragon's own real
  stats give exactly 21, the source's own worked example.
  `find_druidic_monster_assistance()` scans every unlooted, guardian-
  bearing Feature at a province (ascending `feature_id` order), rolls
  each eligible monster's own join chance once, and assigns a random
  0-based battle column on success -- a column an earlier monster in the
  same scan already claimed discards the later one outright, no retry.

  base through two independent uniform draws -- `round(base_points * (1

  threshold -- success raises the skill, failure triggers the same

  failure uses (`_maybe_raise_aptitude()`, reused directly) -- and 100
  is subtracted from the credit either way.

  comatose eligibility gating, which belongs at each future call site's

- **Phase 465**: the real, disassembly-sourced per-turn
  Emperor-election call/coronation evaluation (`AKGEN_reverse_
  engineering_report (2).md` SS13.4/13.6) -- runs every turn
  automatically, regardless of whether any King explicitly asked, unlike
  `can_request_election()`'s own rulebook-literal "un singolo Re...
  alleanza" reading (Phase 228). New `turn/emperor_election.py
  evaluate_election_call(state, requesting_kingdom_ids, current_turn) ->
  ElectionCallOutcome`, implementing the report's own numbered sequence:
  1. find the Kingdom with the single highest `V_k`
  (`_highest_vote_weight_kingdom`, ties keep the lowest Kingdom ID via a
  strict `>` comparison); 2. if its own share of `V_world` already
  reaches the turn-decaying threshold `R`, crown it immediately -- no
  vote, no request needed at all (`immediate_coronation_kingdom_id`);
  3.-4. otherwise sum the weight of every requesting Kingdom
  (`_election_callers_weight` -- the real compiled routine has **no
  alliance concept at all** here, unlike `can_request_election()`'s own
  Phase 228 reading); if that share reaches `R`, `callers_qualify`;
  5. independently, whether any of the 8 "ordinary" Alignments' own
  combined world-power bloc share reaches `R`
  (`alignment_bloc_vote_weights`/`_alignment_auto_trigger`) -- a pure
  Alignment-bloc trigger the rulebook never mentions at all, with no
  Kingdom needing to have "requested" anything. `_alignment_auto_trigger`
  replicates the source's own `alvote` sentinel mechanic precisely: a
  qualifying Alignment **overwrites** a running sentinel while scanning
  in `ALIGNMENT_ORDINAL` order, so the *last* qualifier wins, not the
  first reached or the highest share -- confirmed with a worked test
  where the highest-share Alignment (GOOD, 40%) loses to a
  later-scanned, lower-share qualifier (EVIL, 35%). `requesting_kingdom_
  ids` (every Kingdom whose own `kprevgold` currently holds `VOTE_TURN_
  SENTINEL`, Phase 464's `KingdomMoveHeader.is_vote_turn()`) is the
  caller's own responsibility to assemble from that turn's parsed K1

  wiring" order this module already uses elsewhere. `can_request_
  election()` is kept, unchanged (no other module calls either function
  yet) -- `evaluate_election_call()` supersedes it in spirit, the same
  way Phase 450/451 superseded this module's own original vote-
  weight/win-condition formulas.

  (Valhalla skips normal convocation; Arcane's Valor adds a separate
  3-artifact win condition) -- this project has no `gametyp` concept
  anywhere, the same "no source, no guess" boundary `turn/final_
  standings.py`'s own Phase 454 docstring already drew around `kteam`.

  physical branch that performs the conversion) supplies the exact,
  deterministic formula: not a random roll -- New Rules gives `12 div
  max(1, Total_USkill(target))` (this project has no Old/New Rules
  toggle, so -- the same "New Rules, unconditionally" convention as
  Phase 439/450 -- this is simply *the* formula), where `Total_USkill`
  sums the target's own raw skill level across all 15 `Ability` members

  a King (`LeaderState.is_king` -- an Undead Hero caster never converts,
  `RQ.TXT:3248-3249`), the target not already Undead, and no pending
  Analytical Psychology return recorded for the target. The step loop
  (a `repeat`, not a `for`) always takes at least one alignment-ordinal
  increment and is forced to take one more if it lands on
  `Alignment.ANTI_HOLY` -- Hellish can never be a conversion's final
  resting alignment.

  Undead King charming their own already-loyal Hero purely to trigger
  conversion (the dossier's own case 6) is exactly the scenario the old,
  over-eager marker would have wrongly blocked. Fixed by only setting the
  marker on a genuine cross-Kingdom reassignment (`target.kingdom_id !=
  kingdom_id`).

- **Phase 525**: replaces `turn/encounter.py resolve_fulfill_
  honored()`'s own project-original honor formula (Phase 258, an
  unsourced base-chance/alignment-distance/Evil-penalty model) with the
  exact, now-sourced formula. `AKGEN_reverse_engineering_report (3).md`'s
  dedicated "Dossier FULFILL (FU)" section disassembles the real
  `WillHonor` routine (`AK.OVR:0x194E4-0x1963B`):

  ```
  roll = random_0_99()
  divisor = 1 + Ord(bonus > 0)
  natural   = 20 * abs(6 - monster_align)   ; 6 = Hellish/Anti-Holy ordinal
  mismatch  = 15 * abs(monster_align - hero_align)
  threshold = (natural + bonus - mismatch) div divisor   ; Pascal `div`,
                                                            ; truncated toward zero
  honors = roll < threshold
  ```

  `bonus` varies across the dossier's 24 Quest/reply branches this
  project doesn't model (Phase 258's own scope note -- Fulfill here
  stays the abstract "was the prior Talk's deal honored" roll); every
  call now uses the dossier's own "formula comune" default, `bonus=100`
  (`FULFILL_COMMON_BONUS`). New `fulfill_honor_threshold()` and
  `fulfill_monster_honors()` expose the formula directly (plus the
  RDrain intelligence veto, SS82: `bonus<=0` and a monster smarter than
  Semi auto-betrays, unreachable from this project's own bonus=100 call
  site but kept faithful/testable for a future RDrain-specific phase).
  `resolve_fulfill_honored()` keeps its existing signature/behavior for
  Silver Tongue (Phase 468, still an unconditional always-honors
  short-circuit that also bypasses the veto) and gains optional
  `bonus`/`guardian_intelligence` passthrough parameters. Worked
  examples straight from the dossier (SS80, bonus=100): Worldly(3) vs
  Worldly(3) -> threshold 80 (20% betrayal); Hellish(6) vs Heavenly(0)
  -> threshold 5 (95% betrayal); Evil(5) vs Evil(5) -> threshold 60
  (40% betrayal). A missing `guardian_alignment`/`character_alignment`
  still falls back to `FULFILL_UNRECORDED_ALIGNMENT_FALLBACK =
  Alignment.NEUTRAL` (project-original, not dossier-sourced -- the
  dossier's own formula always has both alignments recorded).
  `turn/search_execution.py _resolve_fulfill()`'s call site needed no
  changes -- the new parameters default to the common-bonus case it
  already wants.

- **Phase 526**: closes the two STEAL micro-gaps flagged
  against `turn/challenge_execution.py` -- both turned out to be
  documentation staleness plus one genuinely fixable formula gap, not
  new mechanics to design.

  **Gap 1 -- Steal not checked as a combat-intent classifier.**
  `has_combat_intent()` (Phase 50) never checks `Maneuver.STEAL`, and
  its own docstring blamed this on Steal being "a separate, still-
  unmodeled tactic." That was true at Phase 50 but stopped being true
  at Phase 305 -- `_resolve_steal_tactic()` has been a real, wired
  branch for many phases now. Re-reading [3.12]'s own English text
  confirms the *behavior* was always correct regardless: "If the
  encounter plan has no **combat tactics or personal combat spells**...
  these restrictions do not apply" scopes the check to combat tactics
  and spells specifically, and Steal is neither -- the module's own
  Phase 305 addendum already established this reading ("Steal's ability
  to fire at all isn't gated on [combat intent]"). No behavior changed;
  three docstrings (module-level, `has_combat_intent()`'s own, and the
  Phase 305 addendum's cross-reference) were corrected via addendum,
  not silently rewritten, to stop claiming Steal is unmodeled.

  **Gap 2 -- the "unresolved" King-vs-army-Hero Steal capture branch.**
  `_resolve_steal_tactic()` returned `"unresolved"` for a King thief
  caught robbing a non-King army-commanding Hero, since neither of
  [5.5]'s two literal capture rules (Hero-thief executed; King-vs-King
  ransom) named that combination. `AKGEN_reverse_engineering_report
  (3).md` SS42 ("Se STEAL fallisce") gives the real compiled capture
  table and pseudocode (`AK.OVR:0x1AC8D-0x1AF99`): a King thief with
  treasury > 0, caught by *either* a King or an army-commanding Hero,
  pays the identical ransom to the victim's own Kingdom; treasury = 0
  executes either way. The real branch condition is only `IsKing
  (thief)` and `victim_is_king_or_army_leader(victim)` -- no separate
  check for whether the victim is personally the King. Merged the two
  branches accordingly: any King-thief capture now pays ransom (or
  executes on an empty treasury) regardless of whether the victim is
  the King or an army-commanding Hero. `"unresolved"` is now reserved
  solely for the pre-existing, structurally different garrison-
  commander case (no `LeaderState` to read from at all).

- **Phase 527**: `turn/expenses.py apply_turn_maintenance()`'s
  own docstring used to say plainly that no bankruptcy/desertion
  consequence was modeled for unpaid leader maintenance, "nothing in the
  available source describes one." Continued reading the same dossier's
  Part II ("reclutamento e mantenimento degli Eroi liberi") turned up
  SS28.1 ("Mancato pagamento e diserzione"), the real compiled
  consequence, disassembled from `AK.EXE:0x1450D-0x14612`: when the
  per-turn payment helper can't fund a specific Hero's own `LCost`, the
  engine rolls `r = (IRand and 3) - 2` (four equally-likely values, -2
  to +1) against that Hero's own `like(hero, king)` -- the identical
  liking value `turn/hire_pay.py required_pay()` already computes for
  pricing, now exposed publicly as `hero_liking()` (was `_like()`).
  `r >= like` deserts the Hero (`kingdom_id` cleared, free to be Hired
  elsewhere); otherwise he stays unpaid this turn ("standby"), no other
  consequence. Desertion probability by `like`: +2 -> 0%, +1 -> 25%, 0
  -> 50%, -1 -> 75%, -2 -> 100%.

  Rewrote `apply_turn_maintenance()`: army maintenance (`ACost`) still
  pays as one unconditional, unclamped lump sum first (no source
  describes an army-side consequence); each non-King, non-Valhalla-
  visitor leader is then paid individually, in ascending `leader_id`
  order (the dossier names no real ordering rule -- ascending id is this
  project's own established "no rule given" tie-break, matching Phase
  451's own vote-order convention), against whatever treasury remains --
  the first Hero the running treasury can't cover, and every Hero after
  them in that kingdom, rolls for desertion/standby instead of being
  paid. Return type changed from a bare `dict[int, int]` to
  `dict[int, MaintenanceResult]` (`debited`, `deserted_leader_ids`,
  `standby_leader_ids` per kingdom) -- the one caller, `turn_processor.py
  run_turn()`, already discarded the return value, so only tests needed
  updating. A kingdom with no recorded King pays unconditionally (no
  `like()` to roll against, same permissive-default convention
  `required_pay()` itself already uses for this exact edge case).

- **Phase 573**: fixed the two real, playability-blocking gaps
  a background audit found while answering "what's missing to make the
  program playable" -- both genuine, not the cosmetic ASCII-map gaps
  the last several phases were about. (1) **`ArmyState.movement_points`
  was never initialized or replenished anywhere.** `worldgen.generate_
  new_game()` built every starting army without it, defaulting to `0`
  (the field's own long-standing comment: "the caller sets it" -- no
  caller ever did), and nothing anywhere reset it between turns either
  -- a real moderator's very first Move order, turn 1 of a freshly
  generated game, would have failed outright. (2) **`state.turn_number`
  was never incremented anywhere in `src/`** -- it stays at its default
  `1` forever across repeated `run-turn` invocations, silently freezing
  every turn-gated mechanic that reads it (Valhalla visitor scheduling,
  Gate Angel due-alignment caching, office-holder turn gates, diplomacy
  first-contact) at turn-1 behavior. Fixed by building the turn-boundary
  reset this project never had: `worldgen/generate_new_game.py` now
  sets each freshly created army's own initial `movement_points` to
  `ARMY_TABLE[army_type].speed`; `turn/turn_processor.py run_turn()` --
  this project's own confirmed "one unambiguous once-per-turn boundary"
  -- now ends every call with a new `_replenish_turn_scoped_state()`
  (refills every army's movement pool the same way, resets `march_
  bonus_applied_this_turn`/`naval_bonus_applied_this_turn`/`unhireable_
  this_turn` to `False`, and `ProvinceState.recruited_this_turn` to
  `{}`) and increments `state.turn_number`. Auditing for the *other*
  "not auto-reset -- the caller's job" fields this project's own model
  comments already flagged turned up 3 more of the same real,
  permanently-blocking bug (an army marked unhireable, or a leader who
  ever benefited from Oratory, or a province that ever hit a recruit
  cap, would otherwise have stayed that way for the rest of the game) --
  fixed alongside the two originally-flagged ones, since they're the
  identical root cause and the fix mechanism was already being built.
  `GameState.gate_angel_candidates_this_turn` was checked and left
  alone -- confirmed already self-resetting via its own direct
  `state.turn_number` comparison, which only needed the `turn_number`
  fix itself to start working correctly. Ran before writing tests: 4872
  passed (non-breaking); one existing test (`test_run_turn_deducts_
  movement_points_for_the_forced_rebattle`) broke because it read
  `movement_points` *after* `run_turn()` returned, no longer a valid
  signal now that the pool is replenished before the call returns --
  fixed to check for the `"forced-rebattle"` `PhaseDispatchResult`
  directly instead, the same signal its own sibling test already uses
  for the opposite case. Added tests: a freshly generated army's own
  full movement pool; each of the 5 reset fields individually via
  `_replenish_turn_scoped_state()`; `run_turn()` itself replenishing
  movement and incrementing `turn_number` end-to-end. Ran again: 4880
  passed (net +8).

  missed_deadline_turn_leaders()` (the real `REPORTS.PAS Set_Defend`
  missed-deadline auto-fill) existed and was tested but was never called
  from `orchestrator.py process_turn()`, so a Kingdom that submitted no
  order file this turn was simply absent from the turn's dispatch instead

  real Kingdom's own move file would report the same value and collide

  the real fix rather than building the missed-deadline wiring on top of
  a known-broken identifier: `HostAK/TP/DEF2.PAS` `Write_Moves`/`Read_
  Moves` both build the move file's own name via `Get_FN('AK', gameturn,

  name the same King ("Uga-Buga Makumb(u)") on their very first line, a

  kingdom_id` property (`models/kingdom.py`) parses this suffix instead;
  `orchestrator.py`/`turn/kingdom_bridge.py` now key off it everywhere
  `kingdom.header.kingdom_number` used to. `Get_FN`'s own body still
  isn't present anywhere in the extracted Pascal source (checked again
  this phase), so the exact byte-level filename-construction algorithm
  remains unconfirmed -- only which value it embeds is no longer a
  guess. `process_turn()` now also builds the missed-deadline auto-fill
  for every Kingdom in `state.kingdoms` missing from this turn's parsed
  order files, merging it into the same `run_turn()` dispatch. Ran
  before writing tests: 4880 passed (non-breaking); one existing sample-
  data test (`test_kingdom_bridge.py`, real `AK3__T1.K1` fixture) had its
  `kingdom_id` assertions corrected from `27` (the old, confirmed-wrong
  `interp_vers` reading) to `1` (the real, filename-derived id); one
  orchestrator test's two-kingdom fixture had its `source_filename`
  fixed to actually vary per kingdom (it had been hardcoded to `"fake.
  K1"` for every kingdom, silently papering over the still-live header-
  based lookup). Added tests: `Kingdom.kingdom_id`'s own filename
  parsing; `process_turn()` auto-filling a Kingdom with no submitted
  order file. Ran again: 4882 passed (net +2).

  -- while about to transcribe `BLUCK2.X2` (`BLUCK.X2`'s still-missing

  sentence after CLUCK's own) -- built from an AKGEN aggregate JSON
  statistic, not a direct `SAY.PAS` citation -- described the wrong
  mechanism. The real code:

      _BLuck: BEGIN
        batluck:= Rint;
        IF Odd(_px+_py+_attl+_defl+_rphase) THEN
            FD('bluck.x2',S_Batt,1000+batluck)
          ELSE FD('bluck2.x2',S_Batt,1000+batluck);
       END;
      _CLuck: BEGIN
        FD('luckint',S_Batt,7);
        IF Odd(_px+_py+_attl+_defl+_rphase) THEN
            FD('cluck.x2',S_Batt,1000+Rint)
          ELSE FD('cluck2.x2',S_Batt,1000+Rint);
       END;

  `BLUCK2.X2`/`CLUCK2.X2` are **mutually exclusive alternate catalogs**
  for the same event, selected by one shared deterministic parity check
  (province x, province y, attacker leader id, defender leader id,
  game phase) -- not a base sentence plus a sometimes-appended
  follow-up. Flagged to the user mid-phase; user chose to correct now.
  Transcribes the real 17-entry `BLUCK2_TEMPLATE`; adds `bluck_cluck_
  uses_secondary_catalog()` implementing the real `Odd(...)` check;
  `render_bluck_event()`/`render_cluck_event()` gain a `secondary`
  keyword driven by it; `render_bluck_narration()`/`render_cluck_
  narration()` now require the formula's five real inputs. Removes
  `render_cluck2_event()` (folded into `render_cluck_event(...,
  secondary=True)`), `roll_cluck_reversal()`, `CLUCK_REVERSAL_INDEX_
  LOW`/`_HIGH`/`CLUCK_REVERSAL_CHECK_PERCENT`/`CLUCK2_REVERSAL_PHRASE`
  outright -- unlike Phase 388's own approximation, this wasn't a
  placeholder for missing text, it was a wrong model of a now-directly-
  confirmed real mechanism, not worth keeping as a "historical record".
  Fixed 5 pre-existing tests that exercised the old reversal-roll
  behavior (`test_battle_luck.py`'s own 3 `roll_cluck_reversal` tests
  and 1 `CLUCK2_REVERSAL_PHRASE` test removed/replaced; `test_turn_
  report.py`'s own 4 `render_cluck_narration` tests rewritten around
  the real parity selector) -- these were the only callers affected;
  neither function was wired into any larger composer yet. Added

  secondary_catalog()` parity coverage. Ran full suite throughout to

- **Phase 610**: wires HostAK/TP/PROSE/DECQ.X/INCQ.X (Phase
  598's own battle quality-change narration) into a real composer,

  `turn/battle_orchestrator.py BattleReport.quality_changes` stored only
  the army's *post*-roll `Quality`, by which point `army.quality =
  roll_quality_change(...)` had already overwritten the pre-roll value
  in place, leaving no way to tell a DECQ (drop) from an INCQ (rise).
  Fixed at the root: a new frozen `QualityChange(old: Quality, new:
  Quality)` dataclass replaces the dict's bare `Quality` value
  (`quality_changes: dict[int, QualityChange]`); all 8 real write sites
  (`_retreat_or_disband()`'s own 2, plus 6 across the attacker/defender
  per-army loops -- winner-improve/loser-decline/fleet-avoids-
  elimination for each side) now capture `old_quality = army.quality`
  immediately before the mutation. New `report/turn_report.py
  describe_quality_changes()` walks the dict, resolves each army's
  display name via the same `build_battle_army_names()` map `describe_
  battle()` already builds, and dispatches to the already-built (Phase
  598) `render_army_quality_decreased()`/`render_army_quality_
  increased()` by comparing `new`/`old` as `Quality`'s own `IntEnum`
  ordinals (`DEPLETED=0` .. `ELITE=5`) -- an unchanged roll (`new ==
  old`) is skipped, since neither template has a real "no change"
  variant. Wired into `describe_battle()` as its own final section,
  after clashes/winner/destroyed/pursuit/retreats. One existing test

  to_depleted_instead_of_destroyed`) updated for the new `QualityChange`
  shape; new tests added for the dataclass's `old`-survives-mutation

  skip rules, and `describe_battle()`'s own wiring. Ran before writing
  tests (non-breaking): 5043 passed. Ran again with new tests: 5047

  `CastExecutionResult.melee_swings` field (mirroring `ChallengeExecutionResult`/
  `PursueExecutionResult`'s own) since `resolve_melee_duel()`'s own
  per-round detail was being computed and discarded.

  **A real, larger, pre-existing bug was found and fixed along the
  way, with the user's explicit sign-off after a direct reproduction**:
  `describe_turn_results()` composes every action's narration only
  after `run_turn()` has fully mutated `state`, so an acting leader (or
  their target) who died as a *result* of their own action was already
  popped from `state.leaders` by the time narration ran. `_leader_
  name()` only checked `state.leaders`, so it silently returned `None`
  for that leader -- and every calling branch's own early-return guard
  then dropped the ENTIRE action's narration, not just the death, but
  every real sentence before it too. Confirmed with a direct
  reproduction (a Challenger who loses and dies got zero turn-report
  lines) before touching any code, then fixed at the root: `_leader_
  name()` now falls back to `state.dead_leaders` (Phase 59's own
  graveyard, the same `LeaderState` object, `.name` untouched by
  death) rather than inventing anything. Fixing this then exposed a
  second, related bug the first one had been silently masking: 3 raw
  `state.leaders[entry.leader_id].location` subscripts (Pursue/
  Challenge/Trail, resolving the *acting* leader's own province for
  `is_sea`/`province_name`) raised a bare `KeyError` the instant
  execution could reach that far for a dead actor -- fixed with a new
  `_leader_location()` helper, the same alive-or-dead fallback.

  New tests: `melee_swings` assertions added to the two existing
  Kill-Enemy-Berserk tests in `test_cast_execution.py`;
  `test_render_kill_enemy_berserk_onset`,
  `test_describe_kill_enemy_berserk_retaliation_returns_nothing_for_an_ordinary_cast`,
  and both winner-direction tests in `test_turn_report.py`;
  `test_describe_turn_results_narrates_kill_enemy_berserk_retaliation_even_when_the_caster_dies`

- **Phase 618**: fixes the real `Maneuver.SAY` decode gap
  Phase 616's own context section flagged -- but the gap turned out to
  be much deeper than "add `SAY` to a frozenset". Reading `HostAK/TP/
  DEF2.PAS` directly (`W_List`/`R_List`) plus the user's own direct
  confirmation established the real on-disk shape: a Search Encounter
  Plan's `SAY` tactic (rulebook [5.4]-[5.8], e.g. "SA-y the character
  number... 'SA Tell me about character 1.'", or the user's own combat
  example `CA-FI, SA "Take that!", FI, ME, ME`) carries free text on its
  own line(s), terminated by a blank line -- not a single following
  integer like `CAST`/`USE_MI`/`GIVE`'s own sub-object. No real sample
  `AK3__T*.K1` file contains an actual `SAY` tactic (already noted in
  `turn/search_decode.py`'s own docstring), so this is built from the
  Pascal source's own confirmed logic plus the user's direct
  confirmation, tested with explicitly-labeled synthetic fixtures, not
  a real byte-level example.

  This isn't just a `turn/search_decode.py` fix: that module only ever
  reads already-parsed `PlanPhase.extra: list[int]` -- pure integers.
  The real gap was one layer down, in `parser/k1_moves.py`/`parser/
  tokens.py`: `_build_leader()` whitespace-flattens a leader's entire
  move block into one flat token stream, discarding line boundaries
  and blank lines before any structural parsing happens -- exactly the
  information needed to know where a `SAY` block's free text ends. A
  real `SAY` tactic would have crashed the parser outright (`consume_
  ints()` raises the instant it hits a non-numeric word), not just
  decoded wrong.

  New `parser/tokens.py flatten_tokens_with_lines()` (returns each
  token's own origin line index alongside the flat stream; `flatten_
  tokens()` is now a one-line wrapper over it, unchanged for its other
  callers). `parser/k1_moves.py` threads this line map (and the raw
  lines) through every phase-parsing function; `_parse_segment()`
  peeks (non-destructively) whether a phase is a Search before choosing
  between the *exact*, untouched `consume_ints()` path (every other
  phase -- what keeps all 10 real `AK3__T*.K1` files byte-identical)
  or a new `_consume_search_extra()`, which walks the tactic list
  `Maneuver`-ordinal-aware and calls new `_recover_say_text()` the
  moment it sees `SAY` -- reading raw lines directly, then resyncing
  the flat token index past whatever it consumed. `_parse_leader_
  blocks()` also had to stop silently dropping blank lines *within* a
  leader block (previously harmless, since nothing needed them) -- now
  kept, since `SAY`'s own blank-line terminator needs to survive into
  `body_lines` at all.

  **A real bug found and fixed while building this**: the first
  version of `_consume_search_extra()` ran its `Maneuver`-ordinal
  classification over *all* of `extra`, including `extra[0]` (`"tl"`,
  always `0`) -- misreading it as a `CAST` ordinal (`0`) and eating the
  tactic list's own real first ordinal as `CAST`'s "sub-object" instead.
  A first synthetic test happened to pass anyway, purely by coincidence
  (`tl=0` and a real leading `CAST=0` landed on the same value); a
  second synthetic test (an *empty* `SAY`) caught it cleanly, since
  there was no such coincidental value collision to hide it. Fixed by
  reading `extra[0]` as one plain int unconditionally, before the
  maneuver-classified walk begins.

  `models/enums.py` gained a public `TACTICS_WITH_SUB_OBJECT` constant
  (promoted from `search_decode.py`'s own private copy, now shared with
  `parser/k1_moves.py` without a `parser/` -> `turn/` layering
  inversion -- confirmed no circular-import risk either way).
  `models/plan.py PlanPhase.extra` widened from `list[int]` to
  `list[int | str]` -- confirmed safe, since every other action type's
  own decoder only ever reads phases of its own action type. `turn/

- **Phase 619**: implements the 8 SA-argument powers this
  project's own roadmap left for last -- the 5 Oracles (`ORAC_ALIGN`/
  `ORAC_POWER`/`ORAC_OFFICE`/`ORAC_GOLD`/`ORAC_TREAS`), `RECHARGE`,

  (user-supplied 2026-08-22).

  New `turn/feature_power_execution.py parse_sa_argument(say_text) ->
  int | None`: tries the whole text as a bare integer first, else the
  first run of digits anywhere in it -- the document gives example
  phrases ("SA Tell me about character 1.") but never states the real
  engine's own text-parsing algorithm, so this is a labeled,
  reasonable interpretation of unsourced *parsing*, not a guess at the
  *mechanic* (which number, and what it does with it, are both fully
  sourced). New `SA_ARGUMENT_POWERS` frozenset, checked by
  `_apply_scout()` (`turn/search_execution.py`) alongside the existing
  `TRACTABLE_POWERS` -- on a full Scout discovery, finds the first
  `SAY` tactic in the plan, parses its argument, and calls `resolve_
  feature_power_attempt(..., sa_argument=...)`.

  Each power reuses an already-built lookup rather than inventing new
  state: `ORAC_ALIGN`/`ORAC_POWER` target a leader id directly (`state.
  leaders`), `ORAC_POWER` reveals `GameState.armies_commanded_by()`'s
  own result verbatim (number + type, not location -- an empty tuple
  is a real "leads no armies" answer, not a failure); `ORAC_OFFICE`
  targets an office ordinal 0-7 (confirmed identical to `Office.
  EMPEROR`..`Office.MAGE`) via the existing `turn/office_holder.py
  resolve_office_holder()` (a vacant office is likewise a real answer,
  not a failure); `ORAC_GOLD` reveals a King's own `KingdomState.
  treasury` -- reconciled a real tension between `FPDESC.X2`'s own
  summary ("Kingdom number") and `POWMSG.X2`'s own operational text
  (which names a character, Hero-vs-King) by reading the argument as a
  leader id whose own Kingdom gets revealed only if they're really a
  King; `ORAC_TREAS` reveals `Feature.treasure` for a target feature id
  (`None` is a real, treasure-less answer with no separate POWMSG id,
  same "no recovered id, narrate nothing" stance as a few Phase
  616/617 outcomes); `RECHARGE` validates ownership and `item.treasure
  in TREASURE_WAND_SPELL` (already exactly the document's own

  applies section 5.6's own deterministic `skill < min(4, aptitude) ->
  skill+1` (distinct from `UP_SKILL`'s probabilistic roll); `GAMBLE`
  rolls two 2d6 totals, a **strictly greater** character roll wins the
  stake, a tie or loss subtracts it (`FPDESC.X2`'s own confirmed
  "tie goes to the house" reading).

- **Phase 620**: closes the user-confirmed-narrow subset of

  candidate(feature_type, feature_index, terrain) -> Spell | None`:

  earthquake()` (already fully built, untouched by this phase) then

  cast time (e.g. a derived `Part_Sea` on Plains, valid at derivation
  since Plains isn't Mountains, but `_execute_part_sea()` specifically
  needs Sea) is a real, sourced possibility this phase surfaces
  honestly as `applied=False`, not something to special-case away.

- **Phase 621**: closes the `miscwrit` gap Phase 620 left
  open. A second, independent reverse-engineering report
  (`miscwrit.md`, user-supplied 2026-08-22) gives `miscwrit`'s real
  shape: a persistent 16-bit bitmask, `GW` header field #33. Its own
  section 7 gives real observed values from this project's own actual
  target data -- `GW3__T1` = `6` (`0x0006`), `GW3__T2`-`T12` = `14`
  (`0x000E`) -- both always with bit `0x0002` set, and `AKGEN.EXE`'s
  own unconditional startup `miscwrit := miscwrit OR 2` (CERTO) gives
  the correct sourced default for a freshly-generated world. Section
  4.2 also supplies `Set_Spell`'s complete, literal `YAK.PAS` source --
  the full outer `REPEAT...UNTIL found` loop and `AnsPrayer`'s own
  "favor White Magic" inner loop, both fully specified now, no bound
  left to guess. With bit `0x0002` confirmed always set in every real
  world this project targets, all 13 of `Set_Spell`'s real candidates
  become resolvable (not just the 3 territory-filtered ones Phase 620
  shipped): `Part_Sea`, `Bless`, `Skeletal_Army`, `Kill_Enemy`,
  `Plague`, `Flood`, `Tornado`, `Earthquake`, `Oratory`, `Clairvoyance`,
  `Illus_Terrain`, `Illus_Armies`, `Hide_Feature` -- all already
  fully-implemented castable spells in `turn/cast_execution.py
  execute_cast()`'s own dispatch, nothing new needed on the casting
  side, only the derivation.

  `models/game_state.py`: `GameState` gained `miscwrit: int = 2`.
  Bits `1`/`4`/`8` (legacy `totfees` fee-migration idempotency
  markers, a diplomacy contact-distribution revision flag) are real
  but belong to entirely unrelated subsystems -- not modeled here.

  `worldgen/internal_magical_locations.py`: new `spell_college(spell)
  -> Ability` (`Set_Spell`'s own `Spell_College(spell, 0)` --
  `_SPELL_COLLEGE_ORDER[spell.value // 4]` for ordinals 0-19,
  `_SPELL_COLLEGE_ORDER[spell.value - 20]` for 20-24 -- cross-checked
  against all 25 spells' own already-confirmed `Ability` scattered
  across `turn/cast_execution.py _SPELL_ABILITY` and `turn/
  encounter.py PERSONAL_COMBAT_SPELL_ABILITY`, zero contradictions).
  `resolve_terrain_spell_candidate()` (Phase 620) replaced by
  `resolve_spell_candidate(feature_type, feature_index, terrain,
  power, miscwrit) -> Spell`: a literal translation of `Set_Spell`'s
  two nested loops -- the inner loop advances `tries` while `tries MOD
  3 != 0` and the college isn't White and `power is ANS_PRAYER`; the
  outer `CASE` dispatch rejects the 12 always-excluded extras, accepts
  `Part_Sea`/`Flood` off Mountains, `Earthquake` off Sea, and every
  other real ordinal on `(miscwrit AND 2) = 2`. Always returns a real
  `Spell` (no longer `Spell | None`) -- proven to terminate, since for
  any terrain at least one of {`Part_Sea`/`Flood` valid} or
  {`Earthquake` valid} is always true (a terrain can't be both
  Mountains and Sea), so the loop can't cycle through all 25 residues
  without finding one; a `_SET_SPELL_MAX_TRIES = 200` defensive cap
  exists purely as a safety net, documented as never actually reached.

  `turn/feature_power_execution.py`: `derive_feature_event()`'s
  `CAST_SPELL`/`ANS_PRAYER` branch now calls `resolve_spell_candidate
  (..., power, state.miscwrit)`. A real, previously-unnoticed
  correctness bug was found and fixed while writing this phase's own
  new end-to-end tests: `_resolve_terrain_spell()` (Phase 620)
  unconditionally targeted the Feature's own province, which is wrong
  for 5 of the 13 real candidates -- `turn/cast_decode.py`'s own
  pre-existing `CHARACTER_TARGET_SPELLS`/`NO_TARGET_SPELLS`
  classification tables show 4 are character-targeted (`Kill_Enemy`,
  `Oratory`, `Clairvoyance`, `Illus_Armies`) and 1 is no-target
  (`Skeletal_Army`). Fixed: the 3 character-targeted spells whose own
  rulebook text explicitly allows self-casting (`Oratory` [4.22.2]:
  "cast on yourself or a co-located character"; `Illus_Armies`
  [4.23.2] similarly; `Clairvoyance` [4.22.3] is inherently
  self-affecting) now target the scouting leader himself;
  `Skeletal_Army` now targets `0` (`cast_decode.py`'s own documented
  "unused" convention); `Kill_Enemy` -- which per rulebook [4.25.2]
  requires the caster to have "desired the death of" a specific,
  player-chosen opponent, impossible in this automatic-cast-on-Scout
  context, and whose rulebook text never describes self-targeting as
  valid -- is refused cleanly with `reason="no automatic target for
  Kill_Enemy"` at the execution layer, not silently miscast and not
  excluded from the derivation formula itself (which stays a faithful
  translation of the real algorithm regardless of what's reachable
  downstream). Found this by trying to write a real end-to-end test
  for a newly-tractable spell (`Oratory`, via a real F#13/Pyramid
  candidate) and discovering `_execute_oratory()`'s own docstring
  contradicted the unconditional province-targeting assumption.

  Report layer: unchanged -- the existing POWMSG 42 template already
  uses `SPELL_NAME[outcome.cast_spell]` generically for any spell.

  target-resolution cases (character-target self-cast, no-target,

  a full `_apply_scout()` cast of `Oratory` onto the scouting leader's
  own army, confirming the target-resolution fix end to end. Ran

  `turn/feature_power_execution.py`: `FeaturePowerEvent` gained `chance_

- **Phase 623**: implements "known provinces" (the user's
  own direct spec, not from a reverse-engineering source this time) and
  wires `Power.MAP_PROV` with it -- closing the Feature -> Power [5.8]
  subsystem's true last gap. A province is known to a Kingdom once that
  Kingdom has at least 1% recorded exploration of it; discovering a
  province (the user's own example: passing by way of an adjacent
  province during Move) acquires it starting at exactly that 1% floor.

  Reuses an existing field rather than adding one: `ProvinceState.
  explored_percent_by_kingdom` (Phase 69) already tracks exactly "how
  much has *this* Kingdom explored this province" -- "known" is simply
  `>= KNOWN_PROVINCE_MIN_PERCENT` (1, `models/game_state.py`, new
  module-level constant). New `ProvinceState.known_to_kingdom(kingdom_
  id)` method (matching this class's own existing `effective_terrain()`
  convention). Confirmed a province an army actually *enters* was
  already guaranteed far more than 1% by the pre-existing partial-
  exploration formula (`turn/exploration.py resolve_explore(...,
  partial=True)`'s smallest possible result, Jungle at skill 0, is 5)
  -- the genuinely new mechanic is revealing a province's own
  *neighbors*, which nobody entered.

  New `turn/move_execution.py reveal_adjacent_provinces(state,
  province, kingdom_id, bounds)`: for each real neighbor (`turn/
  movement.py neighbors()`) of `province` not already known, sets it to
  the 1% floor (never lowers an already-better-known neighbor). Called
  at all 4 existing `record_kingdom_exploration()` call sites (Phase
  69's own module docstring already lists them) -- `move_execution.py
  execute_move()`'s main partial-exploration call and its Map of the
  Marauders sea-vision-extension call, `turn/plan_dispatch.py`'s
  `EXPLORE` branch, `turn/turn_processor.py`'s multi-attacker `LMOVE`

- **Phase 624**: solves the ASCII map's own "far side of the

  PROGRAMMA AK/SE3__T*.K*` corpus (27 real samples with a second map):
  `max_columns_per_page = 78 // cell_stride` (the same 78-char budget
  Phase 577's own Ice-cap dash rule already uses) predicted every one
  of the 27 samples' own real main-map column count exactly, zero
  exceptions -- independently cross-confirmed by the 6 measured strides
  landing exactly on this module's own pre-existing `CELL_STRIDE`
  constants (wide/dense/stride12/10/9/8 -> 4/5/6/7/8/9 columns/page),
  and the wide-tier value (4) matching Phase 567's own separate,
  unrelated correlation finding ("cluster <= 4 always means stride
  17"). Also confirms the board is cylindrical (column 18 borders
  column 1) -- direct visual proof, not inference: `SE3__T10.K1`'s own
  far-side map prints columns 15-18 then 01-05 as one seamless row with
  its own "Ice cap" header, no seam at the wrap -- matching `worldgen/
  place_map.py DEFAULT_WIDTH = 18` exactly. This also explains the
  earlier "falsified" connected-components hypothesis: known, ordinary
  hex-adjacent provinces (`SE3__T4.K6`'s x=17/x=18) can still land on
  different pages, because the split is purely about which page's own
  column budget they fall into, not adjacency.

- **Phase 627**: wires the ASCII map's own layout-*tier*
  selection trigger (`describe_map_report()`, deferred since Phase 567
  -- `report/ascii_map.py`'s 6 real cell-width renderers all existed
  and were tested, but nothing ever picked among them) -- shipped as a
  labeled, **82% (81/99) accurate** best-effort approximation, not a
  solved formula, per the user's own explicit "attempt it anyway even
  if imperfect" direction after two rounds of investigation.

  **The investigation, honestly, including a real methodological
  correction made mid-session**: an early result (a "main-page-only
  column count" measure matching 97/99 real reports) turned out to be
  circular once actually tested against the shipped implementation --
  that measure is *itself* capped by the very pagination formula
  (Phase 624) it was being compared against, so a near-perfect match
  was closer to a restated tautology than an independent discovery.
  Re-tested honestly with a real independent measure (the Kingdom's own
  full, *uncapped* home-anchored cylindrical column cluster -- no
  circular dependency on which tier ends up chosen): **82% (81/99)**.
  Tracing individual Kingdoms turn-by-turn across all 11 real
  `Desktop/PROGRAMMA AK/SE3__T*.K*` samples shows why the remaining 18%
  resists a purely geometric explanation: the real "main page" region
  is a *historical* artifact that grows via genuine, ongoing
  exploration (its own `Expl%` climbs well past the initial reveal),
  then stops for many turns even while a *separate*, equally actively-
  explored "far side of the world" region keeps growing right
  alongside it -- sometimes geometrically *adjacent* to the primary
  region. A single end-of-turn snapshot can measure geometry, not
  history, so it can never fully separate "historically primary" from
  "merely touches the primary region now." Also tried and ruled out:
  total known-column count (same adjacency-conflation problem), widest
  single print row (worse, ~65%), and per-province `Expl%` as a
  "genuinely explored vs. merely revealed" discriminator (directly
  refuted -- far-side provinces show real, substantial `Expl%` growth
  too, not a flat one-time-reveal value).

  New `report/ascii_map.py select_layout_tier(known_columns, home_x,
  board_width=DEFAULT_WIDTH) -> int`: finds the known column closest to
  `home_x` (`KingdomState.home_province.x`, same fallback convention as
  `paginate_known_columns()`), takes its own *uncapped* `_contiguous_
  run_through()` (reused directly, Phase 624), and returns the least-
  dense tier's own `CELL_STRIDE` whose `max_columns_per_page()` covers
  that cluster -- falls back to the `stride8` floor if none does. New
  `LAYOUT_TIERS` registry (least-dense to most-dense, `(CELL_STRIDE,
  render_ascii_map)` through `(STRIDE8_CELL_STRIDE, render_ascii_map_
  stride8)`) shared by `select_layout_tier()` and `describe_map_
  report()`. The 5 previously-unwired renderers (`render_ascii_map_
  dense`/`_stride12`/`_stride10`/`_stride9`/`_stride8`) each gained the
  same `columns: set[int] | None = None` parameter Phase 624 already
  added to the wide-tier renderer, since they're now actually reachable
  in production. `describe_map_report()` calls `select_layout_tier()`
  once per report and uses the chosen renderer/tier for every page
  (matches every real sample: a report never switches tiers mid-report).

  Tests: `tests/test_ascii_map.py` gained 11 -- `select_layout_tier()`
  against a small cluster (stays wide), an exact-fit case per tier, the
  floor-tier fallback, the home-not-known fallback, a real `SE3__T*.K8`
  -shaped primary-cluster-alone case (correct), and a matching case
  demonstrating the function's own documented limitation (a
  geometrically-adjacent-but-historically-separate far cluster still

  each of the 5 newly-wired renderers. `tests/test_turn_report.py`'s
  own Phase 624 multi-page test needed updating: its original 5-column
  fixture now correctly fits on a single, denser (`dense`-tier) page

- **Phase 628**: closes the ASCII map's per-Kingdom
  province-visibility gap -- `render_ascii_map()` and its 5 sibling
  tier renderers previously rendered *every* province in `state.
  provinces`, unfiltered by what the requesting Kingdom actually
  knows, flagged as a real gap since Phase 624 and left open through
  Phase 627.

  **A stale docstring claim was found and corrected while re-checking
  it this session**: `render_ascii_map()`'s own docstring said the map
  "reuses `describe_provinces_report()`'s own visibility convention:
  every province this Kingdom currently has any record of at all."
  Reading `describe_provinces_report()`'s own docstring directly
  (quoting `REPORTS.PAS Rep_Provs`: `IF powner[px,py] = kng THEN ...`)
  shows that report actually filters to provinces this Kingdom
  **owns**, the opposite of "any record of it" -- and an ownership
  filter can't be right for the map either way, since this module's
  own byte-verified real samples show other Kingdoms' provinces and
  `Unowned` provinces printing right alongside this Kingdom's own (the
  map's own real intro text is "a map of all neighboring lands").

  The real, already-sourced concept fits exactly: `ProvinceState.
  known_to_kingdom(kingdom_id)` (Phase 623) -- `explored_percent_by_
  kingdom.get(kingdom_id, 0) >= KNOWN_PROVINCE_MIN_PERCENT` (1%), the
  same "known" concept `Power.MAP_PROV` already uses. All 6 renderers
  (`render_ascii_map`/`_dense`/`_stride12`/`_stride10`/`_stride9`/
  `_stride8`) and `map_region_label()` gained a new `visible_provinces:
  set[HexCoord] | None = None` keyword parameter -- the exact same
  `None`-means-unfiltered shape the `columns` parameter already has
  (Phase 624/627), added as an independent second filter dimension
  (`columns` restricts by x-coordinate for pagination; `visible_
  provinces` restricts by exact coordinate, since a known column can
  still contain an unknown province at a different `y`). `None` keeps
  every one of `tests/test_ascii_map.py`'s own 75+ pre-existing direct
  calls to these functions behaving exactly as before -- zero changes
  needed there.

  `describe_map_report()` (`report/turn_report.py`, the sole
  production caller) now computes `visible_provinces = {coord for
  coord, province in state.provinces.items() if province.known_to_
  kingdom(kingdom_id)}` and derives `known_columns` from that filtered
  set instead of every province that merely exists in `state` --
  meaning `select_layout_tier()`/`paginate_known_columns()` now also
  reflect what the Kingdom actually knows, not just the grid itself.
  Each page's renderer/`map_region_label()` call now passes `visible_
  provinces=visible_provinces` alongside the existing `columns=`
  argument. A freshly generated real game is never left with an empty
  map at turn 0: `worldgen/generate_new_game.py` (Phase 428) already
  seeds a King Home's own province at `explored_percent_by_
  kingdom[owner_kingdom_id] = 100`.

  6 pre-existing `tests/test_turn_report.py` tests needed their
  fixtures updated (province and shared-helper `explored_percent_by_
  kingdom` entries added) once filtering went live for real, since
  none of their `ProvinceState` fixtures previously set that field --
  confirmed by running the suite before writing any new test and
  finding exactly these 6 broke, not left as an assumption. Non-
  breaking check (before any test changes): 5259 passed, 6 failed as
  expected. Tests: `tests/test_ascii_map.py` gained 7 -- a `visible_
  provinces`-filter test per renderer plus one for `map_region_label()`,
  mirroring the existing `columns`-filter tests' own shape exactly.
  `tests/test_turn_report.py` gained 2 -- a Kingdom that knows only one
  of two real provinces renders just that one; a Kingdom that *owns* a
  province but never recorded exploring it still doesn't see it on the
  map, directly exercising the Phase 69/623 "ownership alone doesn't
  imply knowledge" rule this design relies on. Full suite after all
  fixes and new tests: 5274 passed (net +9).

- **Phase 629**: closes the ASCII map's own last open gap --
  the dense and stride-9 layouts' "unexplained margin" Phase 568/571
  found and left unresolved (two real reports directly contradicted
  each other under any single, non-relative pixel-placement formula).

  **The real cause, found by re-reading the actual corpus rather than
  re-guessing**: both "contradictions" are the exact same real
  mechanism Phase 624 already confirmed for pagination -- the board is
  cylindrical, column 18 borders column 1 -- just never applied to
  horizontal cell *placement* before. `SE3__T4.K2`/`SE3__T5.K2` (the
  dense-layout reports Phase 568 couldn't reconcile with `SE3__T2.K1`)
  both have a real known province, `Apurimac`, at `x == 18`,
  cylindrically adjacent to their own `x == 1` cluster; `SE3__T4.K8`
  (the stride-9 report) has TWO, at `x == 17` and `x == 18`, exactly 2
  strides left of its own `x == 1` cluster -- matching Phase 571's own
  already-documented "2 strides" residual exactly. Verified directly,
  character-column by character-column, against every real band in all
  4 previously-contradicting/unresolved reports (not just the samples
  originally checked): once `x_min` is the *true* left edge of the
  report's own cylindrically-contiguous column run, not the raw
  numeric minimum, and the pixel offset is taken modulo the board
  width instead of assumed non-wrapping, all 4 reports match one
  uniform formula with zero residual. `Apurimac`'s own "renders
  immediately adjacent with no gap, not modeled" note (this module's
  own Phase 566 section) is also explained now, not just tolerated: it
  isn't a distant landmass packed in ad hoc, it's an ordinary
  cylindrical neighbor of `x == 1`.

  New `report/ascii_map.py _cylindrical_x_min(columns, board_width) ->
  int`: `_contiguous_run_through()`'s own run (Phase 624), starting
  from the naive `min(columns)`, and returns that run's own first
  element -- the report's true left edge. Reduces to plain
  `min(columns)` whenever no wrap-adjacent province exists, matching
  every already-verified non-wrapping real sample (wide/stride12/
  stride10/stride8's own byte-verified reports never included one)
  unchanged. Every `*_cell_pixel_column()` function (`cell_pixel_
  column`, `dense_cell_pixel_column`, `stride12/10/9/8_cell_pixel_
  column`) now shares one identical formula shape, `((coord.x - x_min)
  % board_width) * CELL_STRIDE + stagger`, and gained an explicit
  `board_width: int = DEFAULT_WIDTH` parameter; `dense_cell_pixel_
  column()` additionally gained the `x_min` parameter it never had
  (Phase 568 left it hardcoded to an assumed `0`, the very gap that hid
  this bug). Each of the 6 renderers now computes `x_min` via
  `_cylindrical_x_min()` instead of a plain `min()`.

  **A second, real bug was found and fixed while wiring this in**:
  every renderer's own row-sort (`sorted(rows_by_y[y], key=lambda p:
  p.coord.x)`) assumed raw `coord.x` order matches pixel-column order
  -- true under the old, non-wrapping formula, but no longer once a
  wrapped province (e.g. `x == 18`) can have a *smaller* unwrapped
  position than a numerically larger, non-wrapped one (e.g. `x == 14`).
  Left unfixed, a wrapped page's own leftmost provinces silently
  vanished from the rendered row (the line-building loop skips any
  cell whose column doesn't exceed the line's current length) --
  caught by re-running the Phase 627 far-side-page test, not assumed
  safe. Fixed by sorting on `(p.coord.x - x_min) % DEFAULT_WIDTH`
  instead of raw `coord.x`, in all 6 renderers.

  Tests: `tests/test_ascii_map.py` gained 5 -- `_cylindrical_x_min()`
  against the no-wrap case (reduces to plain min), the real Apurimac
  case (1 stride), and the real `SE3__T4.K8` case (2 strides); two
  end-to-end renderer tests (dense, stride-9) proving the anchor
  propagates correctly across rows -- the exact scenario the old,
  parameterless `dense_cell_pixel_column()` couldn't even represent.
  3 existing tests updated for the new explicit `x_min`/`board_width`
  parameters (values unchanged, now passed explicitly instead of
  assumed); 1 existing byte-for-byte test's expected padding corrected
  (its own 2-province fixture never included the real anchor province,
  so it now correctly reflects a self-consistent narrower `x_min` --
  see that test's own updated comment); 1 defensive-clamp test updated
  from "clamps to `x_min`" to "wraps to the far side of the board,"
  matching the new modular behavior. Non-breaking check (before any
  test changes): 5274 passed, 6 failed as expected (matching the
  anticipated signature/behavior changes). Full suite after all fixes
  and new tests: 5279 passed (net +5).

- **Phase 630**: wires the last 10 dormant `MeritTally` royal-

- **Phase 632**: closes Move-chase cross-phase persistence
  (rulebook [3.1]). `turn/move_execution.py execute_move()` (Phase 85)
  already resolved a non-adjacent Move target as a chase, one hex-step
  per call -- what was still missing was the rulebook's own multi-phase
  persistence rule: "The movement order will override orders in a
  subsequent phase only if the character is practicing in that phase."
  Two grammatically plausible readings were laid out in that module's
  own docstring (narrow: only a later Practice order is overridden;
  broad: blanket preemption of every subsequent order, mirroring
  Pursue/Trail's own "for the rest of the turn" persistence, Phase 70,
  exactly) -- this project couldn't disambiguate further from the
  available source alone. **The user directly confirmed the broad
  reading.**

  `turn/turn_processor.py run_turn()` now wires this in by reusing the
  exact "PERSISTENT PURSUE/TRAIL CHASE" mechanism already built for
  Pursue/Trail, just simpler: since Move's own chase-stepping already
  lives entirely inside `execute_move()` itself, a continuation is just
  redispatching the *same* ordinary LMOVE phase again with the same
  ultimate target, not a dedicated `advance_*` function the way
  Pursue/Trail needed. New `_ActiveMoveChase` dataclass (`kingdom_id`,
  `target` -- deliberately minimal, since `army_ids` and every
  AdvancedAbility-derived dispatch flag are already re-derived fresh
  from `state` on every dispatch, the same way an ordinary fresh LMOVE
  already works). New `active_move_chases: dict[int, _ActiveMoveChase]`
  in `run_turn()`, checked alongside `active_pursuits` in the same
  preemption filter and continuation-dispatch call. New
  `_continue_active_move_chases()` calls `turn/plan_dispatch.py
  dispatch_phase()` directly (not `_dispatch_single()`, which always
  reports `segment_index=0` regardless of what's passed to it, since
  its own synthetic one-segment wrapper has nothing else to give) and
  builds its own `PhaseDispatchResult` with `segment_index=-1`, the
  same sentinel `_continue_active_pursuits` already uses -- caught via
  a failing test, not assumed correct. New
  `_register_move_chase_continuation()` re-registers a still-unresolved
  chase (`MoveExecutionResult.reached_target` and `.stopped_chasing`
  both `False`) for the next phase, mirroring
  `_register_pursuit_continuation()`'s own shape exactly. Only the
  plain single-leader `_dispatch_single` path registers a chase --
  `_dispatch_multi_attacker_lmove()`'s own grouped-battle path assumes
  an already-adjacent shared target and never calls `step_toward_non_
  adjacent_target()` at all, so extending persistence there is a
  separate, unattempted question.

  Tests: `tests/test_turn_processor.py` gained 2 -- an unresolved chase
  preempting an explicit P1 LMOVE-to-elsewhere order (proving blanket,
  not Practice-only, preemption) and continuing until it resolves, with

  does; a chase that hits `stopped_chasing` (no legal closer neighbor,

  following phase. Full suite: 5289 -> 5291 (net +2).

- **Phase 643**: FINANCES report -- Scientific Treaty
  exchange attribution (`kexch`), the "Received from"/"Sent to" lines

  than that. Richer: there are *two* independent parenthetical lines,
  not one -- `"(Received from player(s) #k1... by scientific treaty)"`
  (`kexch[k1,kng]`) and its own reverse, `"(Sent to player(s) #k1...
  by scientific treaty)"` (`kexch[kng,k1]`) -- each its own separate
  report line, not a same-line suffix. Always "...by scientific
  treaty": this text turns out to be *only* about `turn/scientific_
  treaty.py execute_scientific_treaties()` ([8.4], already fully built)

  discoveries_via_espionage` is deliberately not touched here"). More
  tractable: `kexch[giver,receiver]` is a single value per *directed*
  pair (a real, sourced limitation -- an earlier exchange between the
  same two Kingdoms is silently overwritten, not accumulated), so this
  needed one small new `GameState.discovery_exchanged_from: dict[
  tuple[int, int], Discovery]` field, not the invasive `KingdomState.
  discoveries` data-shape change originally assumed.

  Code`/`Check_DSpab` block was traced and confirmed to produce no
  visible report text at all -- deliberately not modeled, the same
  "internal messaging, not player-facing" stance already established
  elsewhere in this project.

  Tests: `tests/test_scientific_treaty.py` gained 3 -- both directions
  recorded for a mutual exchange, only the real direction recorded for

  recruiting fee sentence, closing the last blocker the 2026-08-26
  codebase survey left open.

  Rulebook [3.4]: recruiting in an ally's territory costs 1 extra gold
  per unit, paid to the ally -- `turn/recruit_execution.py` already
  debited the recruiter and credited the ally's treasury for this
  (`resolution.ally_fee_per_unit`), but the report never said so:
  `RecruitedUnit` only carried the combined `gold_paid` total, with no
  record of whether any of it was an ally fee. The real template
  (`RUMORS.PAS _AAPay`, "< paid # gold to [ for the privilege of

  rendered, blocked on the `[` marker's own referent: the real
  `Imp_Code(_AAPay)` trigger call doesn't survive in any of the 13
  available `.PAS` files, only the message-table declaration and
  `SAY.PAS`'s own `Say(...)` text do -- so whether `[` names the ally
  King or reuses the sibling `_ARecr` message's garrison-commander/
  `Pronoun()` convention couldn't be settled from source alone.

  **User-confirmed directly**: `[` is the ally King's own name. New
  `RecruitedUnit.ally_fee_paid: int` (Phase 645) carries the real fee
  per unit, set from `resolution.ally_fee_per_unit` in
  `execute_recruit()` (already 0 outside ally territory, so no extra
  gating needed). `report/turn_report.py` gains `render_recruit_
  ally_fee()` (the new template) and `_ally_fee_recipient_name()`
  (resolves the province owner's King via the existing `_king_leader_
  id()`/`_leader_name()` helpers, Phase 217/612, falling back to the
  Kingdom's own name in the unreached edge case of no recorded King).
  `describe_recruit()` appends the `_AAPay` line right after a unit's
  own RECRUIT.X/HIREMERC.X sentence whenever `ally_fee_paid` is set --
  applies to both a freshly levied and a hired-mercenary unit alike,

  territory with no `hired`-based exception.

  territory case asserting `ally_fee_paid == 0`, plus an assertion

- **Phase 646**: CHARACTERS report's mercenary hire-cost
  hint (`Desc_Stranger`'s own `IF lstate[ldr]=Mercenary...` block) --
  closes the last item flagged in the 2026-08-26 codebase survey.

  `REPORTS.PAS`: `IF lstate[ldr] = Mercenary THEN IF LCost(ldr,kng) <=
  3 THEN IF LKing(ldr) = noleader THEN` -- when an impulse-2 stranger
  (a wandering Hero this kingdom knows the location of) would cost 3
  gold or less to hire, a second line appears: "(who, we hear, desires
  to enter thy Majesty's service for N gold per annum)". `lstate`'s
  own *write* side (what sets a leader's real engine-side condition to
  `Mercenary` in the first place) has no surviving source anywhere in
  the 13 available `.PAS` files -- previously flagged as needing "a new
  state concept... no matching concept anywhere in `GameState`".

  That framing turned out to be incomplete: `turn/hire_pay.py hero_
  liking()` (Phase 505, built from a *separate* disassembly-based
  dossier of `AKGEN.EXE`/`AK.OVR`) already answers this exact question
  for the very same real `LCost` formula this hint calls -- its own
  `temper_conflict` term reads "hero is still Mercenary (unhired)" as
  `hero.kingdom_id is None`. Reused directly rather than re-derived:
  `_render_stranger_row()` now renders the hint whenever the impulse-2
  target is a *live* (`leader.leader_id not in state.dead_leaders`,
  since `Dead` and `Mercenary` are mutually exclusive real `lstate`
  values), kingdomless leader whose `turn/expenses.py leader_pay()`
  (the same "Pay" formula the impulse-1 table's own column already
  calls) is 3 gold or less. `LKing(ldr) = noleader` becomes redundant
  under this reading and isn't checked twice. No new `GameState` field
  needed -- `LeaderState.kingdom_id is None` already existed.

  Tests: `tests/test_turn_report.py` gained 7 -- `_render_stranger_
  row()` shows the hint for a cheap kingdomless Hero, omits it above
  the 3-gold threshold, omits it for a dead kingdomless Hero, omits it
  for a leader with a kingdom, and never shows it for impulse 3
  (structural, not incidental); `describe_characters_report()`
  end-to-end shows the hint right after the ability-description line,

  gets it. Full suite: 5407 -> 5414 (net +7).

- **Phase 647**: Skeletal Army "digs its own grave" on
  Leave/reassign, found by a fresh codebase survey after the 2026-08-26
  one closed out.

  Rulebook [4.2.5], quoted in full: "Se chi lancia l'incantesimo cerca
  di abbandonare l'Esercito di Scheletri o di affidarlo a un altro
  personaggio, che non sia un Re Non-Morto, gli scheletri soldati si
  scaveranno da soli la tomba e riprenderanno il loro sonno
  interrotto." -- leaving a Skeletal Army uncommanded, or handing it to
  anyone but an Undead King, destroys it outright (not a demotion to
  ordinary mercenary status, the way Disband works). `turn/skeletal_
  decay.py`'s own module docstring already flagged this as "still
  unmodeled -- a different, uncommanded-army rule."

  Both trigger halves (abandon, reassign-to-non-Undead-King) collapse
  to one check in `turn/plan_dispatch.py _dispatch_leave()`: new
  `_is_undead_king(state, leader_id)` -- a King (`is_king=True`) whose
  own *Kingdom's* `Alignment` is `UNDEAD` (kingdom-alignment-based, the
  same eligibility gate `turn/merit_points.py _king_of_alignment()`
  already established for the differently-scoped `Office.UNDEAD_KING`
  title, reused for consistency rather than re-deriving a possibly-
  different "personal alignment" reading) -- returns `False` for
  `leader_id=None` too, so both trigger halves share one branch. A
  matching army is removed via `GameState.remove_army()` instead of
  reassigned; `ArmyListExecutionResult` gains `skeletal_army_lost:
  list[tuple[int, ArmyType]]` (captured before removal, since the
  army no longer exists in `state.armies` by report time). The real
  `_ADig` message (`RUMORS.PAS` id 4012, `SAY.PAS`: "= dug graves for
  themselves, unwilling to serve anyone but their master, unless given
  to an Undead leader like themselves.") has no surviving `Imp_Code`
  trigger call in any of the 13 available `.PAS` files -- the same
  class of gap `_AAPay` had before Phase 645 -- but unlike `_AAPay`
  there's no ambiguous marker to resolve (just `=`, the army
  designation), and the rulebook text gives the full trigger condition
  directly, so this is fully sourced end to end despite the missing
  trigger call. Whether the lost units re-enter `GameState.battle_
  graveyard` (available to a future Skeletal Army cast) is genuinely
  unresolved by this text and deliberately left unmodeled, same "no
  source, no guess" stance as everywhere else in this project.

  Tests: `tests/test_plan_dispatch.py` gained 9 -- `_is_undead_king()`
  for `None`/unknown/non-King/non-Undead-kingdom-King/Undead-kingdom-
  King; `_dispatch_leave()` for abandonment, reassignment to a non-
  Undead King, reassignment to a real Undead King (survives, command
  transfers normally), and an ordinary non-skeletal army left
  uncommanded (non-regression). `tests/test_turn_report.py` gained 3 --
  `render_skeletal_army_dug_grave()`'s own template text; `describe_
  leave()` rendering the `_ADig` line alone and after an ordinary LEAVE
  sentence. Full suite: 5414 -> 5426 (net +12).

- **Phase 649**: BATLDR.X -- a King/Hero personally commanding
  a battle -- the 3rd candidate from the fresh survey that found Phases
  647/648, re-scoped once its real trigger was read in full.

  `SAY.PAS:1028-1048` (`_BLeaders`/`_BLList`, read in full for the first
  time this phase) turned out to describe something simpler than the
  pre-existing "per-column front-rank position" framing assumed: for
  each battle side, a real roster of leaders present, split at a cutoff
  (`cdrdex[fn]`) into those who actually command an army (get the
  BATLDR sentence) and those merely present leading nothing (`"< was
  there, leading no armies."`). Not a battle-line-position model change
  after all -- the "commanding" half is data this project already
  computes and discards: `turn/battle_orchestrator.py`'s own army-
  grouping-by-`commanded_by` step (`_select_side_commander()`) already
  builds the full candidate list before picking just the winning
  Supreme Commander.

  New `BattleReport.attacker_commanding_leader_ids`/`defender_
  commanding_leader_ids: list[int]`, computed directly in `fight_
  battle()` from `attacker_armies`/`defender_armies`' own distinct
  `commanded_by` values (sorted, deduped) -- independent of `_select_
  side_commander()`'s own internal candidate list, so no signature
  change needed there. A united multi-attacker battle (`fight_multi_
  attacker_battle()` calls `fight_battle()` once per merged group, its
  own `combined_army_ids` already spanning every party) naturally
  recovers every commanding leader across the whole side for free.
  `report/turn_report.py describe_battle()` renders one BATLDR sentence
  per id (attacker's own roster, then defender's), silently skipping
  any id that no longer resolves in `state.leaders` -- placed first,
  before BLUCK, matching `SAY.PAS`'s own real dispatch order.

  **Deliberately still not modeled**: a leader present at a battle but
  commanding no armies at all (`tentdex[fn] > cdrdex[fn]`) -- this
  project's battle model has no way to know a leader was physically
  present without also commanding at least one of the armies actually
  fighting, for either battle path.

  Tests: `tests/test_battle_orchestrator.py` gained 4 -- `fight_
  battle()` records both sides' real commanders; excludes unled armies;
  dedupes/sorts multiple commanders on one side; a united multi-
  attacker battle recovers commanders from both parties.
  `tests/test_turn_report.py` gained 2 -- `describe_battle()` renders
  the BATLDR lines first, attacker roster then defender; a commanding
  leader no longer in `state.leaders` is silently skipped. Full suite:
  5433 -> 5439 (net +6).

  REPORT" table -- the very first thing `Pray_Report` ever prints,

  found and fixed well over a dozen times. The fix is one new field
  (`ElectionResult.ballots`), not new cross-turn state machinery.

  `ElectionResult` gains `ballots: dict[int, int]`, set at all 3 of

  parameter (default preserves every existing caller unchanged).

  table: `[]` unless `election_outcome` is a real `ElectionResult` (an
  `ElectionCallOutcome` means no vote was tallied this turn). One row
  per `sorted(state.kingdoms)` -- that Kingdom's own King (`_king_
  leader_id()`, "no King" fallback), its own cast weight (`kingdom_

  one" for an abstainer -- the real `kprevgold[k2]=No_King` case),
  votes received (`votes_by_candidate`), and a percentage. **The
  percentage uses real `Trunc()`** (`int(votes_received / total_votes_
  cast * 100)`), confirmed directly against the actual source line
  quoted above during this phase -- not the `round()` this phase's own
  written plan had second-guessed itself into proposing (the plan's own
  Context section had already correctly transcribed `Trunc()` from the
  source; its Design section then mistakenly hedged toward `round()`

  immediately before whichever of that function's own two `imperial_
  office_lines` call sites fires this turn (both are the same real
  `Pray_Report` procedure call, just repositioned pre/post-election per
  Phase 561) -- matching the real source's own position, the very first
  content that procedure prints.

  **One deliberate simplification, documented not guessed**: the real
  "Neutral Characters `<tottax-tktax>` No one" row (world tax base
  belonging to no Kingdom at all) is omitted entirely -- `total_votes_
  cast` (`V_world`) has no concept of tax base *outside* Kingdom

  base" quantity feeding the election-weight formula. Revisit if a
  future source clarifies what that figure means in this project's own

  from [[project_large_gap_survey_2026_08_27]], the last piece of that

  Encounter default remain a separate, larger, explicitly-deferred

  own module docstring already states plainly they "share exactly the

  phases exist in any sample), and the new SEP decoder. `parser/
  k1_moves.py`'s own `_parse_segment()` widens its Search-only peek to
  also cover `ActionCode.CHALLENGE`/`PURSUE`, and parses `SP:` itself
  unconditionally via the shared walk (no leading action code to peek
  at -- `SP:` is always tactic-list-shaped). Every real sample stays
  byte-identical (confirmed by running the existing suite unchanged
  first) -- this only changes behavior for input no real sample has
  ever exercised, the same precedent Phase 618 itself set.
  `PlanSegment.sp` widened from `tuple[int, ...]` to `tuple[int | str,
  ...]`, mirroring `PlanPhase.extra`'s own Phase 618 widening.

  New `turn/sep_decode.py`: `decode_special_encounter_plan()` (the
  bare tactic-list decode, no leading `tl` slot to strip -- confirmed
  absent from `SP:`'s own real grammar); `plan_intent()`, a literal
