- **Phase 673**: a second reverse-engineering document,
  `Desktop\BOLD OK.txt` (2026-08-29, requested directly to check
  whether it "chiarisce le idee" on monster intimidation), supersedes
  Phase 671/672's own project-original formula and narration with the
  real, CERTO-level compiled mechanism.

  **The real intimidation trigger is a per-damage-packet, independent
  roll** (`AK.OVR` raw `0x1651A-0x16607`), not Phase 671's own end-of-
  combat total-loss approximation: `p(d,t,m) = min(1, d*(4-t)/
  mtbasehp[m])` for every packet of damage `d` a `Bold` guardian takes,
  where `t` is its current combat Temper ordinal and `mtbasehp[m]` is
  the species' own base HP constant (`MONSTER_RUNTIME_PROFILE[monster].
  average_hit_points`, the same value Phase 670's own raid-damage
  formula already uses). The first successful packet sets a sticky
  per-encounter flag, applied to `guardian_state` only at the
  encounter's own closure. New `turn/monster_raids.py intimidation_
  packet_chance()`/`roll_guardian_intimidation()`, replacing Phase
  671's own `guardian_intimidated_by_combat_damage()` entirely.

  **A second real outcome this project never modeled**: `_MUnDt` --
  "wounded but undeterred" -- fires when the guardian took real damage
  but no intimidation packet ever succeeded, and it's still `Bold`. No
  state change. New `turn/monster_raids.py guardian_undeterred()`
  (pure predicate) and `SearchExecutionResult.guardian_undeterred`.

  **Independent confirmation, not just new claims**: BOLD OK.txt's own
  seasonal `Bold`-promotion algorithm (its section 6) reconstructs the
  exact same 3%/Worldly-Animal/`Calm->Mercenary->Bold` mechanism Phase
  670 already built independently from THUNDERBIRD.md -- real, external
  confirmation that `age_feature_guardian()` needed no changes at all.

  `turn/search_execution.py _resolve_search_encounter()` gains one new
  local closure, `_resolve_guardian_pacification()`, replacing all 7 of
  Phase 671's own call sites at once -- it rolls the real formula
  against every Melee swing/Fire Arrow shot the leader landed on the
  monster this encounter (`MeleeSwing`/`FireArrowShot`, Phase 415/175's
  own already-granular per-hit records, reused directly with zero new
  tracking), then checks `_MUnDt`'s own precondition if not intimidated.
  Deliberately still out of scope: threading other damage-dealing
  spells (Fireball, Ice Suspension, Telekinetic Storm, Holy Symbol,
  Spiritwrack) into the packet list -- this module's own combat model
  resolves most of them as outright kill-or-continue, not a discrete
  non-fatal damage number, and auditing each one individually is a
  separate, larger follow-up.

  **The literal English `Say()` text for all three of Phase 672's own
  project-original report lines is also recovered**, wired verbatim:
  `_MNoBold` ("< was intimidated by the encounter..."), `_MUnDt`
  ("In > judgement, < was undaunted..."), and `_LPacif` ("in ]
  gratitude/Rappreciation, [1 swore off any raids..."). Each event's
  own real `Imp_Code` call passes only ONE entity (the monster/Feature
  itself), confirmed directly from both documents' own pseudocode --
  so every person-marker in all three templates (`<`, `>`, `[1`, `]`)
  resolves to that same single monster, not a second (leader) actor,
  even though `[`/`]` are this project's own general "second character"
  convention elsewhere. New `_search_province_name()` resolves the real
  `@` province name via `result.request.feature_id` -> the Feature ->
  its province, falling back to "these lands" when unresolvable.

  other half, "if the character doesn't command any armies, the

  already-proven monster-plan combat model (Phase 293) rather than
  giving the target's own plan only a pre-combat veto.

  New `turn/sep_decode.py target_uses_special_encounter_plan(state,
  target_leader)`: `True` iff the target is a real `LeaderState`
  commanding no army (`GameState.armies_commanded_by()`), the literal
  rulebook condition.

  `turn/challenge_execution.py resolve_challenge_combat()` gains an
  opt-in `target_tactics: list[SearchTactic] | None = None` parameter
  (default `None` reproduces every existing caller/test byte-for-byte
  -- confirmed by running the full suite unchanged before writing a
  single new test). When given, the target's own plan gets a second
  tactic cursor (`_peek_target_cast()`/`_advance_target_tactic()`/
  `_target_has_more_casts_pending()`, ported branch-for-branch from
  `search_execution.py`'s own monster-plan quartet), consulted by a new
  per-round dispatcher covering all 4 real combinations: the target's
  own leading Casts resolve before combat starts
  (`_resolve_target_casts()`); a target Cast mid-Melee-round takes the
  place of its own reactive swing, itself subject to the caster's own
  counter-swing and disruption check; a Cast-vs-Cast round resolves
  both sides' own spells with no swings; and a target with any Cast
  still pending disables both existing atomic fast paths (the lone/
  last-Melee shortcut and the exhausted-tactic-list tail), forcing the
  round-stepped path so a later Cast is never skipped. `execute_
  challenge()` and `execute_pursue()`'s own armyless-case call site
  both compute `target_tactics` via the new eligibility check and
  thread it through.

  **Two real, precedent-driven scope narrowings, found while
  designing, not guessed**: (1) `Maneuver.FLEE` stays unwired for
  *either* side in this engine (already a separate, documented gap for
  the caster's own Flee) -- giving only the target Flee-via-SEP agency
  here would be a new inconsistency, not parity, so the target's own
  scope stays Cast-timing agency only, exactly matching what Search's
  monster-plan engine already grants its own passive side. (2) No new
  "does the target want to Shoot" gate is needed -- Fire Arrow's own
  `resolve_fire_arrow_duel()` already resolves a fully bidirectional
  exchange in one call regardless of either side's plan, unlike
  Search's monster side, whose *canned* plan might omit Fire Arrow
  entirely.

  Two real bugs found and fixed while writing the new tests, not
  assumed away: a `_resolve_melee_round()` draw-vs-continue conflation
  (a genuine atomic-duel draw and "round undecided, keep walking" both
  collapsed onto the same `None` return value, causing `resolve_melee_
  duel()` to be invoked twice in one scripted-draw test) -- fixed by
  widening the return to `tuple[bool, str | None]` (`encounter_over`,
  `outcome`); and a stuck-cursor bug where the target's own Melee peek
  never advanced its own tactic index, risking an infinite loop once a
  later Cast was queued behind it -- fixed by calling `_advance_target_
  tactic()` explicitly in that branch, mirroring `search_execution.py`'s
  own identical, already-commented precedent for its Melee-vs-Melee
  round.

  `turn/turn_processor.py _dispatch_mutual_encounter()` needed no code
  change at all -- it already calls `execute_challenge()`/`execute_
  pursue()` rather than `resolve_challenge_combat()` directly, so the
  non-initiator's own real plan is picked up automatically; proven end
  to end (not just by inspection) with a real mutual-Challenge fixture
  where an otherwise-losing target's own leading Cast (`SP: 0 <spell>
  -1`, genuinely decoded via the existing per-turn SEP-decode pass)
  flips the winner.

  The user resolved the one remaining open design question directly:
  the exchange is one-sided (the target gets no return fire -- no
  Archery is possible at Spell Range without the ability -- and no
  melee counter, too far away; only a Cast counter, already resolved
  independently and upfront by this same function regardless of
  range). `turn/encounter.py resolve_fire_arrow_duel()` gains a new
  `long_range_archer` parameter (default `None`, every existing caller
  unaffected) that forces the other side's shot count to zero and
  applies a flat `LONG_RANGE_ARCHERY_HIT_MULTIPLIER = 0.5` to the
  named side's own hit chance. Deliberately still open, each flagged
  rather than silently dropped: `AdvancedAbility.SHORT_RANGE_ARCHERY`
  (fire at Melee Range) is a genuinely separate question the user's own
  answer doesn't cover (a target there stands right next to the
  archer, so whether they get a reactive Melee counter needs its own
  confirmation); `turn/search_execution.py`'s own separate, duplicated
  `CombatRange`/`SHOOT` state machine (leader-vs-monster Search combat)
  is untouched. Test count: 5862 -> 5870 (net +8). Full suite verified
  green (unchanged, 5862) before writing a single new test; every new
  test passed after accounting for this shared function's own existing
  "exhausted tactic list defaults to Melee" tail fallback needing a
  mocked `resolve_melee_duel()` alongside the mocked `resolve_fire_
  arrow_duel()` in three of the new tests.

- **Phase 701**: `AdvancedAbility.SHORT_RANGE_ARCHERY`,
  closing the category's last open question: "the Archer may now use
  the Fire tactic at Melee Range, with the normal chance to hit." The
  user resolved the design question directly, choosing a reactive
  Melee counter-swing over no counter at all: unlike Long Range
  Archery's fully one-sided exchange, a target at Melee Range stands
  right next to the archer, so it gets a free reactive Melee swing
  against the archer first (mirroring this same function's own
  existing Cast-at-Melee-Range reactive-swing branch) before the
  archer's own shot resolves one-sided, at normal (not halved) accuracy
  -- matching this ability's own text exactly, since it never mentions
  a reduced chance the way Long Range Archery does. `turn/encounter.py
  resolve_fire_arrow_duel()` gains a new `short_range_archer` parameter
  (default `None`, every existing caller unaffected), sharing the same
  one-sidedness mechanism as `long_range_archer` but applying no hit-
  chance multiplier. `turn/challenge_execution.py resolve_challenge_
  combat()`'s own `[5.0]` Melee-Range block for `Maneuver.SHOOT` now
  checks for the ability before falling back to its existing outright
  block. `turn/search_execution.py`'s own separate, duplicated
  `CombatRange`/`SHOOT` state machine (leader-vs-monster Search combat)
  remains untouched, same as Phase 700. Test count: 5870 -> 5877 (net
  +7). Full suite verified green (unchanged, 5870) before writing a
  single new test; every new test passed on the first run.

- **Phase 702**: `AdvancedAbility.THIEF_TREASURY_RAIDS`,
  closing backlog item #11 -- [5.5]'s own "if the victim is a King,
  there's a possibility of stealing gold from him (depends on how much
  he has in the treasury)" clause had a real mechanic but no magnitude
  anywhere, until this ability's own text supplied "the thief gets away
  with up to half of the treasury." A successful Steal against a
  foreign King now redirects to a gold raid instead of item theft (per
  [5.5]'s own "oro o... oggetti" -- gold OR items, not both). Two real,
  user-confirmed design decisions round this out: (1) the thief may
  satisfy co-location by standing in the target King's own still-owned
  home province instead of the King's literal hex ("even if the thief
  is in the king's home province while the king is elsewhere"); (2)
  `execute_challenge()`'s own King-refusal gate is bypassed for a real
  Treasury Raid attempt, mirroring `SPY_ASSASSINATE`'s own unconditional-
  accept precedent (Phase 698) -- without it, an ordinary one-sided
  Challenge against a King is refused unless `mutual_encounter=True`
  (rare), contradicting the ability's own "activated by giving an order
  to Encounter that king number" framing. A real, previously-documented
  "consciously-not-fixed" gap (Phase 305/306) blocked the most natural
  plan shape and got fixed alongside it, generally, not just for this
  ability: a Steal-only plan (no Melee/Shoot/Cast) used to bypass
  `resolve_challenge_combat()` entirely, silently never firing Steal at
  all -- confirmed safe by direct trace (every existing `combat_
  occurred=False` test uses a Talk-only plan, never Steal). Two
  interpretation choices for the ability's own unsourced magnitudes,
  both user-confirmed: "up to half" is a uniform random fraction between
  0% and 50% of the treasury (`turn/encounter.py treasury_raid_amount()`);
  "the guard is doubled... against further attempts" cumulatively
  doubles per attempt this turn (`KingdomState.treasury_raid_attempts_
  this_turn`, a `2 ** attempts` multiplier stacking on top of the
  existing King-target halving). Pursue's own separate co-location/
  acceptance logic is deliberately untouched (the ability's own text
  names "Encounter," [3.12] Challenge specifically) -- `gold_raided`
  still reaches through Pursue's armyless case "for free" via the
  shared `resolve_challenge_combat()` core. Test count: 5877 -> 5895
  (net +18). Full suite verified green (unchanged, 5877) before writing
  a single new test; every new test passed on the first run.

- **Phase 703**: the 5 "_PLACES" Advanced Abilities
  (`HOLY_PLACES`/`DARK_PLACES`/`ELEMENTAL_PLACES`/`PSYCHIC_PLACES`/
  `ILLUSORY_PLACES`) -- identically worded per magic school, e.g.
  `HOLY_PLACES`: "At any Monastery, Altar or Great Hall, the success
  chance to cast a White Magic spell is increased by 20%. For Search
  Feature actions, the 20% bonus is applied when that type of feature
  is searched. For Action spells, the bonus is applied if that feature
  type is in the same province as the character, and is not occupied
  by a monster." Two genuinely different formulas, two genuinely
  different wiring points, sharing one `PLACES_ABILITY_FOR_ABILITY`/
  `PLACES_FEATURE_TYPES` table pair (`turn/cast_execution.py`): the
  Action-Cast half (`_roll_cast_success()`, new `_caster_holds_places_
  bonus()`, +20% additive alongside the two Pagan bonuses) requires the
  matching Feature to be *unoccupied* ("not occupied by a monster,"
  read as `guardian_monster is None or looted` -- a dead guardian's own
  species stays recorded, only `looted` flips); the Search Feature half
  (`turn/search_execution.py`'s own Cast-tactic resolver, `turn/
  encounter.py resolve_personal_combat_spell_cast()`'s new `places_
  bonus` parameter) has no occupancy condition at all -- Searching a
  Feature already means targeting that exact one, guarded or not.
  Corrects a stale docstring: `cast_execution.py`'s own Phase 387 note
  had flagged `places_of_power_bonus_percentage_points` as one of "4
  more real spellcasting rules deliberately NOT wired" -- 2 of those 4
  (`damp_magic`/`damp_college`) turned out already done since Phase
  617, never updated; only `combat_slots_per_school` (a per-encounter
  cast-count limiter) remains genuinely open. Test count: 5895 -> 5913
  (net +18). Full suite verified green (unchanged, 5895) before writing
  a single new test; every new test passed on the first run, after one
  real implementation bug caught before it shipped: `Feature`'s own
  field is `kind`, not `feature_type` -- fixed immediately, before any
  test was written against it.

- **Phase 704**: `AdvancedAbility.ENHANCED_EARTHQUAKE`, the
  Tidal Wave -- "when an Earthquake is cast on a Sea province... every
  military unit... has a 5% chance per level of the spellcaster of
  being destroyed (except for Whales and Sea Folk)... the tidal wave
  will continue on, moving generally in the opposite direction from
  the spellcaster... weakening by 5% upon entering each new province...
  when it finally hits a land province, it will end there, but will be
  effective against Fleets, Sea Folk and Whales (only)... If the wave
  hits the Ice Cap, it simply ends there." `_execute_earthquake()`
  previously rejected Sea targets outright -- this ability is the real
  capability gate that lets a caster target Sea at all, not an
  unmodeled edge case of the base spell. Every named piece reuses
  existing project data rather than inventing new tables: "Whales and
  Sea Folk" is `models/army_type.py OVERFLIGHT_SEA` exactly; "Fleets,
  Sea Folk and Whales (only)" is the identical `SEA_ARMY_TYPES`; "Ice
  Cap" needs no new check at all -- a propagation step running off the
  map or onto a coordinate with no `ProvinceState` already means
  nothing further to hit, the same structural dead end the rulebook's
  own flavor text describes. Two new small `turn/movement.py` helpers,
  `neighbor_in_direction()`/`direction_between()`, drive the wave's own
  straight-line stepping via the existing `Direction`/offset tables
  (Phase 89); `turn/cast_execution.py` gains `_apply_tidal_wave_step()`
  (one shared per-province destroy roll for both the Sea and land
  phases) and `_propagate_tidal_wave()` (the stepping loop). Two
  design decisions confirmed directly with the user: a same-hex
  fallback (caster co-located with the Sea target, e.g. aboard a
  Fleet, so there's no real "away from the caster" vector) picks a
  uniformly random `Direction`; and the wave keeps physically moving
  through Sea provinces even after its own destroy chance has decayed
  to 0%, until it genuinely reaches land or the map's edge, matching
  "when it finally hits a land province, it will end there"'s own
  definite-arrival framing. New report-layer narration is deliberately
  out of scope (no source text found beyond the already-wired, terrain-
  agnostic "@ was devastated by an earthquake!" bystander notice, which
  needs no change). Test count: 5913 -> 5923 (net +10). Full suite
  verified green (unchanged, 5913) before writing a single new test;
  every new test passed on the first run.

- **Phase 705**: `AdvancedAbility.SPY_EXPANDED_SPYING` --
  "When using the Spy Province action, the Spy gains information on
  what features are known to the owning kingdom. With the Trail
  action, estimates are gained for skills, and for offices held." Two
  of the three clauses reuse infrastructure the eleventh through
  sixteenth surveys' own picks already built: the Spy Province half
  (`turn/aspy_execution.py execute_aspy()`, new `SpyReport.features_
  known_to_owner: dict[int, int]`) reports whatever real discovery
  level (1-3) *the province's own owner Kingdom* has recorded per
  `Feature.discovered_by_kingdom` -- deliberately the owner's own
  level, not the caster's -- for every Feature there the owner has
  discovered at all, mirroring `caster_has_druidic_animal_spies`'s own
  Phase 694 shape exactly. The offices-held half (`turn/trail_
  execution.py execute_trail()`/`advance_trail()`, new `TrailExecution
  Result.offices_held: tuple[Office, ...]`) resolves fresh via `turn/
  office_holder.py resolve_all_office_holders()`, filtered to whichever
  real (leader-scoped) Offices the target currently holds -- read as an
  exact fact, not a perturbed Spy Table estimate, since office-holding
  has no real magnitude to add a margin of error to. The third clause
  (skill estimates) stays genuinely unmodeled: no `Skill_Est` routine
  survives anywhere in the source (unlike `Align_Est`/`Temper_Est`),
  so inventing one would be a guess, not a recovery -- flagged
  explicitly in both functions' own docstrings, not silently dropped.
  Test count: 5923 -> 5934 (net +11). Full suite verified green
  (unchanged, 5923) before writing a single new test; every new test
  passed on the first run.

- **Phase 706**: `AdvancedAbility.SENSE_DANGER_TALENT` --
  "The Psychic is able to sense the approach of dangerous enemies and
  can avoid unwanted encounters, both random ones and with unfriendly
  characters. Encounters with unfriendly characters can be avoided 50%
  of the time. It is used only when the Flee tactic is the first one in
  the special encounter plan." Only the "unfriendly characters" half is
  modeled -- this project has no random-encounter-generation mechanism
  at all (confirmed by the SEP roadmap's own earlier investigation), so
  the "random encounters" half stays honestly unmodeled, flagged rather
  than silently dropped. New `turn/challenge_execution.py target_
  evades_via_sense_danger(state, target, challenger)` pre-combines
  ability possession, `not state.is_allied(...)` ("unfriendly"), and
  the target's own real Special Encounter Plan leading with `Maneuver.
  FLEE` (reusing `sep_decode.py sep_accepts_challenge()`, Phase 669,
  inverted -- already exactly this condition; `target_uses_special_
  encounter_plan()`, Phase 674, gates whether an army-commanding
  target's SEP is even in play at all, same as every other SEP
  consumer). `is_encounter_accepted()` gains `has_sense_danger_
  evasion`, checked only right before the function's own final,
  unconditional "Heroes who don't lead armies can always be
  Encountered" fallback -- deliberately scoped narrower than every
  other branch above it (King target, army-leader target, King
  challenger), since [3.12]'s own text carves no exception into any of
  those more specific rules. Wired into all 3 real call sites
  (`execute_challenge()`, `execute_pursue()`'s armyless case, `execute_
  patrol()`) via the new pre-combined predicate, since the ability's
  own text names "encounters" generically rather than scoping to one
  order type. Test count: 5934 -> 5948 (net +14). Full suite verified
  green (unchanged, 5934) before writing a single new test; every new
  test passed on the first run.

- **Phase 707**: random-encounter generator primitives, new
  `turn/random_encounter.py`, sourced from a new user-supplied reverse-
  engineering document (`CASUALENCOUNTER.md`) describing the game's
  random-encounter system: after Move/Explore/Search/Pursue/Trail,
  there is a real per-terrain chance of an encounter with either a
  reskinned "patrol" or a genuine wandering monster drawn from the full
  60-species table with a real, non-uniform weighting formula
  (`100/HP²`, plus a two-table habitat filter). Closes a real,
  previously-confirmed-genuinely-blocked gap: `AdvancedAbility.SENSE_
  DANGER_TALENT`'s own "random encounters" clause (Phase 706) had no
  mechanism to hook into until now. `MONSTER_RUNTIME_PROFILE[monster].
  average_hit_points` (Phase 381) matches the document's own `mtbasehp`
  table exactly, all 60 entries -- reused directly, no new HP table.
  Two genuinely unrecoverable Pascal internals, user-confirmed rather
  than guessed: the patrol diplomatic-safety check (`rel + Rand2 >= 2`)
  maps this project's own binary `is_allied()` to Allied=always-safe/
  Neutral=50% (not "not allied = never safe" -- matches the rulebook's
  own "twice as safe" framing the document itself quotes); the
  "traveling with an army" escort exclusion is approximated as "a
  same-Kingdom army physically present at the destination coordinate."
  **Primitives only -- not yet wired into turn dispatch.** Two real,
  scoped follow-ups: Phase 708 (dispatch wiring, the ephemeral
  synthetic-monster representation, combat-engine integration, closing
  Sense Danger Talent's own clause in full) and Phase 709 (the full
  pre-combat outcome tree and report-layer wiring, including the
  already-built-but-unwired `render_wandering_encounter()`/`render_
  patrol_release()`/`render_patrol_encounter()`, Phase 106/107). Test
  count: 5948 -> 5985 (net +37). Full suite verified green (unchanged,
  5948) before writing a single new test; every new test passed on the
  first run.

- **Phase 708**: random-encounter dispatch wiring, synthetic
  monster, combat integration, and `AdvancedAbility.SENSE_DANGER_
  TALENT`'s own "random encounters" closure. New `turn/random_
  encounter_execution.py`. The one open architectural question from
  Phase 707 (how to resolve combat between a leader driven by their
  own real Special Encounter Plan and a bare `Monster`) resolved by
  direct investigation, not guesswork: no monster-side plan generator
  is needed at all -- `turn/challenge_execution.py resolve_challenge_
  combat()` already fully supports a synthetic, no-real-`LeaderState`
  opponent (`target_leader=None`, a bare `Combatant` for `target`),
  already a real production path (`turn/battle_orchestrator.py`'s own
  Duel/garrison-commander reuse) -- the monster becomes a purely
  reactive, passive opponent, matching the document's own "the base
  combat engine is the ordinary shared one" framing exactly. `monster_
  combatant()` builds a `Combatant` from a bare `Monster` value alone
  (confirmed: `MONSTER_COMBAT_STATS` covers all 60 real species, zero
  gaps). Sense Danger Talent's own random-encounter clause reduces to
  the existing `sep_decode.py sep_accepts_challenge()` primitive
  (Phase 669) at a fixed 100% (not 50%) since the opponent is
  synthetic. Wired into `turn/plan_dispatch.py run_leader_plan()`'s
  own per-phase loop, right after each phase's ordinary dispatch, for
  exactly the 5 real triggering action types. **Deliberately deferred
  to Phase 709, not silently skipped**: the document's own SS12
  pre-combat social-outcome decision tree (`approach_score` and 8
  named branches) is not modeled yet, so every non-evaded encounter
  currently goes straight to combat -- more often than the real game
  would; report-layer narration is also entirely Phase 709's own
  scope. Test count: 5985 -> 6010 (net +25). Full suite verified green
  (unchanged, 5985) before writing a single new test; every new test
  passed after one fix found while writing them -- `tests/_helpers.py
  ScriptedRandom` doesn't control `rng.randint()` the way it controls
  `.random()` directly (Python's `_randbelow` fallback still reads
  `.random()` internally in this environment, but needs a real queued
  value, not an empty script) -- fixed by buffering a few extra
  scripted values on every test that reaches real `Combatant`
  construction rather than by controlling the exact roll.

- **Phase 709**: report narration for exactly what Phase 708
  already models -- a failed terrain roll (`_LNoRand`), the encounter
  opening (`_LREnc` + `_LWEnc`/`_LPEnc`), a diplomatically-safe patrol
  release (`_LSafe`), and the combat outcome. Re-reading the document's
  own SS12 ("Decisione prima del combattimento") closely found it's
  thinner than initially assessed: the `approach_score` formula that
  gates the avoidance branch depends on two Pascal "local" values whose
  meaning is confirmed unrecoverable, and -- more importantly -- the 8
  named social-outcome branches (`_LPass`/`_LBefr`/`_LTricks`/`_LDense`/
  `_LDona`/`_LHear`/`_LNice`/`_LGreet`) have no recoverable selection
  formula at all, only names/ids/flavor text. **User-confirmed
  directly, presented with this finding**: don't attempt that tree
  (genuinely unrecoverable without inventing a whole sub-mechanic) --
  it's recorded as a permanent, genuinely-blocked backlog item, not a
  deferred phase. Two fully-sourced renderers built but never wired
  since Phase 106/107 (`render_wandering_encounter()`/`render_patrol_
  encounter()`/`render_patrol_release()`) are finally reached; two new
  single-template renderers transcribed verbatim from the document's
  own SS16.1. A real, easy-to-miss SS16.5 detail confirmed and applied:
  once an encounter is framed as a patrol, the opponent's own species
  name is replaced with "the Officer" in combat narration. New
  `describe_random_encounter_combat()` deliberately doesn't reuse
  `describe_encounter_combat()` verbatim (that function also renders a
  Steal sub-line with no sourced/meaningful application against a
  synthetic monster) -- a smaller sibling reusing the same Fire-Arrow/
  Melee/death renderers instead. Sense Danger evasion gets no
  resolution sentence of its own (no distinct `_L`-code survives for
  it) -- only the encounter's own opening narrates, a real, flagged
  gap. Test count: 6010 -> 6025 (net +15). Full suite verified green
  (unchanged, 6010) before writing a single new test; every new test
  passed on the first run -- each render/describe function's own exact
  output was verified empirically (a live Python call, not predicted)
  before being written into an assertion, avoiding any guesswork about
  the prose-template mini-language's exact resolution semantics. This
  closes the entire Random Encounters roadmap.

- **Phase 710**: comment-only, no behavior change. Fixes the
  last open item from the seventeenth fresh codebase survey: `turn/
  strength.py`'s own module docstring still claimed Illusory Terrain's
  blended-strength averaging was unbuilt because "no spellcasting
  system exists yet"/"no item-effect system exists at all" -- both
  false (spells since Phase 3, item effects since Phase 141). The
  identical claim in `models/game_state.py` was already caught and
  narrowed in Phase 683, but `strength.py`'s own copy was never updated
  to match -- a fresh recurrence of the "stale known-gap claim"
  pattern. Narrowed to the real, still-genuine gap: no exploration/
  movement mechanic distinguishes real vs. illusory terrain for
  combat-strength purposes (the illusion's only real consumer today is
  report-layer narration). Full suite unchanged (6025).

- **Phase 711 (current)**: wires `describe_battle()` (leader roster,
  monster assistance, luck lines, per-column clashes, destroyed/
  pursuit/retreat, quality changes) into the real letter-report
  pipeline for the first time -- it had been fully built and tested
  since much earlier phases but never called from production. Picked
  from the eighteenth fresh codebase survey. A direct investigation
  found this more tractable than the survey's own initial "large, own
  roadmap" estimate: army naming (the survey's own flagged concern)
  turned out to already be fully solved (`build_battle_army_names()`,
  wired since Phase 236), and the one genuinely missing piece --
  retreat destination names -- needed only one new `BattleReport` field
  (`retreat_destination_coord`), populated at the exact point `fight_
  battle()` already computes the value and previously discarded it.
  **User-confirmed directly**: both Kingdoms actually involved in a
  battle (not just the acting side) receive the identical, full
  narrative in their own ACTION REPORT -- the turn's own `results` list
  is keyed by the acting leader alone, so this needed a genuinely
  different, turn-global threading mechanism (new `record_battle_
  narratives()`, mirroring `record_battle_world_events()`'s own "called
  once per turn" shape, populating a new `GameState.battle_narratives_
  by_kingdom` dict read directly by `compose_letter_report()`) rather
  than an extension of the existing per-entry `describe_turn_results()`
  walk. The existing one-line world-broadcast summary (`record_battle_
  world_events()`) is untouched -- both mechanisms coexist by design,
  one thin-and-broadcast, one rich-and-personal. Test count: 6025 ->
  6030 (net +5, plus one existing `test_battle_orchestrator.py` test
  extended in place). Full suite verified green (unchanged, 6025)
  before writing a single new test; every new test passed on the first
  run, with one real assertion built empirically (a live Python call
  verifying the exact retreat-line/army-naming interaction, not
  predicted) after finding `build_battle_army_names()`'s own docstring
  claim about `retreated_army_ids` needed a fixture with a real battle
  column, not just the id list alone.

## Setup

```
cd ak_engine
python -m venv .venv
.venv/Scripts/pip install -e ".[dev]"   # Windows
pytest -v
```

than guessed, to avoid silently encoding a wrong interpretation. Each will
need cross-referencing against `HostAK/TP/DEF2.PAS` (`Read_Moves`) and the
rulebook before being turned into named, typed fields:

- ~~`KingdomMoveHeader.raw_fields[1]` and `[2]` — vary between turns (0/1
  and 0/8/1020 observed); meaning unknown.~~ -- **half-stale as of a
  Phase 410-607 re-audit (Phase 609)**: **Phase 464** gave every
  `raw_fields` slot a named, sourced identity (`allreq`=`[1]`,
  `brreq`=`[2]`, etc.), cross-confirmed against `DEF2.PAS Write_Moves`/
  `Read_Moves`'s own field order two independent ways -- "which Pascal
  field is this" is closed. **Genuinely still open**: the *semantic
  value* those two fields hold is still unconfirmed -- `models/
  kingdom.py`'s own current docstring: "not further decoded...
  presumably an alliance-request value... but that reading is
  unconfirmed."
- `PlanSegment.sp` (the `SP:` field) — meaning unknown; always ends in the
  values seen in samples but not confirmed to always be a fixed shape.
- The exact meaning of the 31 integers on the skill-values line — expected
  15 ability pairs (30 values) based on `CTBOTH.PAS`'s `ability` enum, but
  every real sample file has exactly 31. The 31st value's meaning is
  unconfirmed; `SkillTable.pair_for_ability()` only interprets the first 30.
- ~~`parser/k1_moves.py` mis-parses a nested Hire/Charm/Resurrection
  plan~~ **fixed in Phase 18** — see that phase's note above for the

  ~~A Cast-triggered nested plan's `ActionPlan.leader_id` is always

  spell, so a Charm/Resurrection cast's own target -- the nested
  character's real id -- is recoverable). ~~Nothing decodes/executes a
  nested plan's own contents~~ **fixed in Phase 23 (decode) and Phase 32
  (dispatch)** — see Phase 32's note above; a newly-hired or
  Charm-targeted character's own orders now dispatch the same turn.
- ~~**Hex adjacency scheme** (`turn/movement.py`) — the original adjacency
  code isn't in the available source (it lived in the missing main
  program). The module implements a standard "odd-r" offset hex grid,
  which is consistent with the 6 direction names confirmed in
  `CTBOTH.PAS` (`dirname`), but the exact offset convention is a guess and
  unverified. Revisit here first if movement behavior ever looks wrong
  against real game data.~~ -- **resolved by Phase 314**: the exact
  offset-to-parity convention is now confirmed directly from real
  `Desktop/SE3__T*.K*` turn-report narrative text (5 real provinces, 15
  individual direction observations, zero contradictions) -- see that
  phase's own note above for the full sourcing and the one-line parity
  fix it required (`neighbors()`'s own ternary, plus `_to_cube()`
  switching from "odd-r" to "even-r" to match).
- **Humanoid-army-type compatibility** (`models/army_type.py`
  `MONSTROUS_ARMY_RACE`) — the rulebook states plainly that monstrous army
  types (Dragons, Eagles, etc.) require their own race's province, and
  that any humanoid army type works in any humanoid province, but never
  says explicitly whether a *humanoid* type can be recruited in a
  *non-humanoid* (monstrous) province. This module assumes not (symmetric
  incompatibility) — a reasonable reading, not a verified rule.
- **"Beasts" nemesis matchup** (`models/army_type.py` `NEMESIS`) — the
  rulebook lists "Beasts" as a nemesis type for Lt/Hvy Cavalry and
  Chariots but never defines the term. Interpreted here as `{Elephants,
  Camel Corps}`, the table's two mounted "beast" units — a guess, not a
  quote.

  hits the first anchor exactly but gives 80%, not "assured", at 4:1 — an
  approximation flagged in the function's docstring, not a sourced
  formula. Revisit if a real battle result ever contradicts it.

  a local `U[0,1)` draw per side, combined via `R_s = 1 +
  k*(G_s+L_s)` (`k` = 0.75 turn 1, 1.5 later), always applied, no
  "does it trigger" gate at all -- verified by a 2,000,000-draw Monte
  Carlo check against the source's own declared probability tables
  (within 0.03pp, sampling noise). The real BLUCK/CLUCK narration text
  itself was recovered too (Phase 388, from `AKGEN`'s own
  `battle_engine` catalogs). See `turn/battle_luck.py`'s own module
  docstring for the full derivation.

  unlike every other assumption in this README, this one is backed by an
  empirical test against real move-file data, strengthened in Phase 315:
  width=10 now scores 84.7% (50/59) against `turn/movement.py`'s Phase
  314-confirmed adjacency parity, and is the decisive best fit across an
  exhaustive width sweep from 2 to 200 (next closest: 57.6%) -- far above
  the ~1-2% expected by chance. Phase 315 also ruled out one plausible
  alternative: AK3 LMOVE targets are NOT SE3-style `row*100+col` province
  numbers (23.7% match), despite both filename families sharing a "3".
  Still open: the exact board height (real data reaches y=17, taller than
  `turn/movement.py`'s assumed 15-row "normal" board -- this game series
  may simply use a different board size), which row-parity convention
  applies (genuinely too close to call from AK3 data alone -- 50 vs. 52
  of 59 -- though `turn/movement.py`'s narrative-sourced convention is
  used here too, being the stronger evidence), and what the ~15% of
  non-adjacent pairs represent (some are plausibly legitimate, e.g. a
  leader chasing a distant target; one suspiciously round jump, exactly
  170, might be a distinct sentinel value).

  **stale as of Phase 405 (written at Phase 316, when this really was

  - **The 128-row block**: Phase 316's own "falsified" verdict was
    itself later reversed. A further reverse-engineering pass (working
    from a direct disassembly of the original `AKGEN.EXE`

    `GWFeatureRecord` -- confirmed 14-for-14 against every Feature
    named in 8 real provinces' own letters (guarding `Monster`,
    `FeatureType`, `Treasure`, and per-coordinate row count all match
    exactly). The "ruled out, not just unconfirmed" framing this
    bullet inherited from Phase 316 was true only until Phase 341.
  - **The 218-row block**: confirmed **per-army, not per-Hero** (Phase
    317 already overturned Phase 316's own "one row per Hero" reading
    before this bullet was written) -- a Hero can have many rows the
    same turn, one per commanded army. All 10 fields are now decoded
    into a real `GWArmyRecord` (Phases 331-337): commander, coordinate,
    Race, `ArmyType`, `Quality`, `MonsterEngagementState`, a Skeletal/
    mercenary marker, movement points, a death/transformation marker,
    and a plague-survival counter -- not "7 still-unresolved trailing
    fields."
  - **The kingdom/leader header block**: has a full parser
    (`parse_gw_leaders()`/`GWLeaderRecord`, Phases 316-330 plus the
    `AKGEN.EXE`-sourced Phase 343 addendum) -- name, race, alignment,
    temper, condition, coordinate, skills, kingdom/Liege resolution
    (Hero via the Liege field, King via file order, both confirmed
    against real letter rosters), birth coordinate, hiring turn, all
    three Imperial Office merit tracks, Sage/Priest merit, an
    experience accumulator, and several rarely-nonzero moderator/
    bookkeeping fields. Each leader's own `"Action Plans:"` block (the
    part this bullet called out by name) is real and already
    machine-parseable in the exact same grammar `parser/k1_moves.py`
    already uses. The world file's own 33-field header is fully decoded
    too (`parse_gw_header()`/`GWHeader`, Phase 342).
